items.title: kwb-model has no identity scheme, and every content-addressed thing above it is waiting on one
items.why: The .NET prototype's DeterministicId (SHA-256 into a UUIDv8, with a claim's SourceId deliberately excluded from the hash) is the actual cross-source dedup mechanism: two books asserting the same claim hash to the same id, so a second admission is an upsert rather than a duplicate. D17 and D18 in that prototype's own AGENTS.md are both failures that a stricter identity discipline at the type level would have made harder to reach — a merge that fused two distinct concepts, and a predicate fed into an algorithm that assumed a property it did not have. This item is the decision point for which of those become type-level invariants here rather than review conventions. Measured 2026-09-12 by KWB-9, detail in docs/corpus/prototype-inventory.md: the prototype's identity discipline was implemented once and applied almost nowhere — 87 types in Domain/ default their Id to Guid.NewGuid(), against 9 files that call DeterministicId, and the twelve byte-identical epistemic kernel nodes are all in the first group. DeterministicId.From(params string?[]) is itself the bare static this item's done_when forbids, which is how the discipline became forgettable. Four design details are worth carrying whole and are recorded in the inventory: the version-8 UUID tag rather than an impersonated v5, the 0x1F separator chosen because whitespace normalisation cannot produce it, case deliberately not normalised, and a null part kept distinct from an absent one. D20 belongs here too: the prototype declares `public double Confidence { get; set; } = 1.0` in 40 Domain types (41 counting one init), so an unset confidence reads as certain — the unfinished half of that prototype's own ADR 0001 follow-up, whose value objects (Confidence, RigorLevel, AccessibilityLevel) sit in Domain/Values alongside the 40 bare doubles.
items.done_when: kwb-model exposes a content-derived identity type whose construction requires the bytes it is derived from (no bare `new` that accepts an arbitrary string), documents which fields participate in the hash and why, and has tests demonstrating that two inputs differing only in an explicitly-excluded field (the source) produce the same identity.

items.title: kwb-store has no write door, and D19/D20 in the prototype are exactly the failure a missing one allows
items.why: D19 (a scheduler defaulted queued work to Succeeded when its handler did not exist) and D20 (an enum's zero-value default read as success) are both failures of a status being assumed rather than derived from evidence. kwb-store's own write door is where a status becomes a property of what was actually written, not a value a caller could construct optimistically.
items.done_when: kwb-store exposes one write path whose result type cannot be constructed as successful without the bytes it wrote, mirroring the one-write-door discipline nomos-store documents in f:/repos/nomos.

items.title: The universal epistemic type kernel is named in every document about this product and designed in none of them
items.why: The .NET prototype's Domain/Universal — a discipline-neutral type and relation hierarchy that domain-specific YAML packs specialize — is the piece the prototype's own architecture treats as most load-bearing. Porting its type *tree* (the ~30 hardcoded UniversalType entries) without re-deriving why its relation kinds are the closed set would be porting the easy half and leaving the actual design decision unmade here. CORRECTED 2026-09-12 by KWB-9, measured in docs/corpus/prototype-inventory.md: this item previously said 'nine relation kinds'. UniversalRelationKind has 21 members — nine cross-domain discovery discriminations plus twelve structural families (Taxonomic, Compositional, Dependency, Logical, Evidential, Normative, Representational, Functional, Temporal, Contextual, Contradiction, Contrast). An implementer who re-derives only the nine re-derives the vocabulary of discovery and inherits unexamined the vocabulary that types every relation the packs actually declare. Three further measurements bear on this item. First, the prototype's real answer to D18 is not the nine kinds but UniversalRelationKindExtensions.Constraint() — a per-kind algebra commitment checked by AlgebraViolations on the pack-load path (DomainPackValidator.cs:196 from DomainPackRegistry.cs:86) — and that is Exercised, whereas the node types are only Declared and Implemented per D-003. Second, twelve types implementing IEpistemicNode are byte-identical apart from the type name, and six of them reach no consumer at all, so they are one hypothesis expressed twelve times rather than twelve concepts. Third, nine hand-written IDomainModule implementations (1,430 lines) have zero consumers outside their own directory and are kept in sync with the YAML packs by a drift test that is their only reader — do not rebuild the twin. Of a pack's seven declared contributions only the relation algebra reaches the runtime, and ValidationConstraint carries a prose Description with no predicate, so no pack validation constraint can fire.
items.done_when: kwb-domain states, as a record, what a UniversalType hierarchy must guarantee (closed under IsA, one KnowledgeLayer per type) and what the relation vocabulary must guarantee — for all 21 kinds, not only the nine discovery discriminations: that they are complete and mutually exclusive, or a documented reason they are not, and what algebra each kind commits its specializations to — before any domain pack format is designed against it.

items.title: kwb-ingest has no admission pipeline, and the prototype's own D18 is what happens when one is built without re-deriving its algorithm's assumptions
items.why: D18 fed a pairwise-correct IsVariantOf predicate into union-find, which assumes transitivity the predicate did not have, and fused distinct concepts through bridge terms in 25% of merges — undetected by 1,878 passing tests, because they tested the predicate and not the consuming structure. Building admission here is the point to re-derive, for every algorithm used, what property it actually needs from its input rather than assuming one that happens to hold on the test corpus.
items.done_when: kwb-ingest implements link-concepts, normalize-concepts and admit in that order, and each stage's tests exercise the algorithmic property that stage's design depends on, not only its typical-case output.

items.title: kwb-retrieval and kwb-mcp have no query surface, and the prototype's mutation-exclusion decision (its own D10) is not yet a property of this workspace's types
items.why: The prototype's MCP host exposes nine read-only tools with every reply bounded so an agent cannot exhaust its own context, and excludes mutation from that surface entirely. Read this as a contract worth preserving independent of the protocol carrying it: the type an MCP tool handler is built against should not have a mutating method to call by mistake. The nine tools are confirmed by measurement (search, get_concept, neighbours, path, proofs_for, claims_for, code_for, gaps_in_source, list_connection_hypotheses). KWB-9 attaches a second incident to this item, detailed in docs/corpus/prototype-incidents.md as D19-B: the prototype's AGENTS.md carries two distinct incidents both numbered D19, and the second one — 'a filter that applies itself is a check nobody asked for' — is the one its own ROADMAP does not carry forward. Its subject is which world a read returns. A global query filter rewrote every query including ones written by people who had never heard of it, so merge-audit resolved none of the merge log's ids against the current view, printed 'nothing has been merged away' and exited 0 — every merge on record could have been wrong and the gate would have passed. No filter at all failed the other way. The prototype's answer is two interfaces (IConceptRepository current, IConceptHistory every version) so that needing retired rows is a dependency visible in a constructor, liveness is one expression rather than three hand-written copies, and an audit carries an independent expectation and throws rather than reporting a zero. That is the same structural discipline this item already states for mutation, applied to temporality; two read types, not one type with a flag. A second observation, measured against nomos 2026-09-12 and detailed in docs/corpus/nomos-as-precedent.md, bears on the second half of this item: nomos-mcp holds a tool CATALOGUE and no protocol. Its ServedTool names which tools exist, the sentence each publishes and the schema each accepts, while the whole initialize/tools-list/tools-call/ping handshake, notification suppression and framing come from xvpe-remote-call-backend-json — its own band entry states the test that the split was drawn correctly, that 'this crate names no protocol library at all'. The prototype's nine tools are a catalogue in exactly that sense. Whether this repository may take that edge is KWB-8's question, not this item's; what this item can take from it either way is that the protocol is not the part worth owning, and read-only-ness is.

items.title: This repository has a work/ledger.json and no tool that operates on it
items.why: AGENTS.md documents claim, finish, and territory as this repository's coordination mechanism, but nomos-ledger — the crate that actually implements those verbs in f:/repos/nomos — is Nomos-specific by location, not by semantics; ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 already names it a candidate whose subject does not require the thing being coordinated to be software. D-135's new default-to-XVPE policy for genuinely domain-neutral code makes this the first real test of that policy in practice, not a hypothetical. The absence now has a concrete victim: KWB-9 ran to completion and could not be finished through the ledger, because AGENTS.md forbids hand-editing an item to Done and no tool exists to transition it any other way. It is therefore parked in Claimed with its artifacts delivered — which is exactly the state this item exists to stop being the only available one. Measured against nomos 2026-09-12, detail in docs/corpus/nomos-as-precedent.md: this decision has a cheaper fourth option than the three named above, and a different governing record than the one named below. The fourth option is to adopt nomos-ledger's SCHEMA without adopting any dependency. Running nomos's own binary against this board — `nomos work validate` from this repository's root — reads this file, parses it, and refuses it at exit 5 with `missing field kind`. Field by field the two schemas are one: Territory is identical (resolution/paths/patterns), ItemState already includes Claimed, and abandoned/displaced/declined are already here. The entire gap is two closed-set fields (kind: capability|decision|validation|correction|cleanup, origin: required|proposed) and schema_version 1 against nomos's 5. Both containers use serde(deny_unknown_fields) per OD-LEDGER-008, which is why the refusal is total rather than partial. On the governing record: D-135 decides where NEW domain-neutral code is authored and is explicit that it does not weaken the proof requirement for code moving after the fact, so evaluating D-135's admission test against nomos-ledger evaluates the wrong test — nomos-ledger is 14,008 lines of existing code, and the clause that governs moving it is D-122 as adopted into ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001: two products demonstrating materially identical domain-neutral semantics. This board being nomos's schema minus two fields is close to that proof and is materially stronger than the hypothetical D-122 exists to refuse. Two bounds: XVPE has no work-ledger crate today (xvpe-frame-ledger is timing, xvpe-task-* is runtime concurrency), and nomos already measured Territory as a migration candidate and rejected it under OD-PLATFORM-003's criterion — no XVPE site was found doing it worse. That criterion asks what XVPE is missing and is silent on what a second product needs, which is this item's actual question. Finally, the mechanism this repository most concretely lacks is the lease: nomos's claim lapses, `list` reports it lapsed rather than claimed, and Take_Over recovers it while preserving the displaced claim. KWB-9 being unfinishable is that absence, measured. CLAIM NOTE, moved here by KWB-13 because nomos-ledger's Claim carries holder and timestamps only: Claimed 2026-09-12, territory narrowed from [docs/records, work] to [docs/records] on release: `work` was needed only to claim this item and to add KWB-13, and holding it afterwards blocked KWB-13 — the item that finishes this one. That is OD-LEDGER-001's authoring mistake, made for the second time in one session on this board, which is itself evidence for what D-005 decided. Decision recorded as D-005: adopt nomos-ledger's schema, use its binary as the interim tool, and defer ownership. The three options this item named are all about owning ledger code; measurement showed the question was wrong-shaped, and the two options it did not name are the ones that answer it. KWB-13 is the follow-on the decision implies. Parked in Claimed rather than Done for the same reason KWB-9 is: no tool exists to transition it, which is this item's own subject. KWB-13 landing is what makes both transitionable.
items.done_when: A decision exists, recorded here, on whether this repository's ledger tooling vendors nomos-ledger, depends on a shared XVPE crate D-135 would place it in, or forks one — made by evaluating D-135's own admission test against this concrete case, not by defaulting to whichever is easiest to start.

items.title: The XVPE dependency hazard rests on a compile failure that no longer reproduces, and a stale premise is not permission to take the dependency
items.why: AGENTS.md refuses a path dependency on f:/repos/xvpe because its foundations tier does not compile, citing xvpe-dataflow at 62 errors as of the last check from the Nomos side. Measured 2026-09-12 from the xvpe workspace, `cargo check -p <crate>` exits 0 for xvpe-primitives, xvpe-serialization, xvpe-sync-primitives, xvpe-collections, xvpe-algorithms, xvpe-dataflow, xvpe-math, xvpe-formula and xvpe-json-text — xvpe-dataflow itself finishing with 106 warnings and no errors. That measurement covers libraries only: no tests, no --all-targets, and no doctests, which `check` never compiles. So the hazard's stated premise no longer reproduces, and that says nothing about whether the position it supports is still right: Nomos's own D-130 may rest on reasons the compile failure never carried, and a build observation is not an architecture decision. The failure this item exists to prevent is someone reading a green `cargo check` as permission. The observation this item carries — that the premise is stale — is settled, and measurement against nomos on 2026-09-12 found it stale a SECOND way, which the compile-check never touched. Detail in docs/corpus/nomos-as-precedent.md. AGENTS.md and README.md here both refuse the dependency 'for the same reason Nomos's own D-130 gives', and OD-PLATFORM-003 retired that clause for this crossing: 'No, for the XVPE crossing. Nomos is built on top of XVPE. XVPE is the engine. This workspace is an application over it, in the same sense the knowledge workbench is.' That record characterises THIS repository's relationship to XVPE, not only its own. It closes exactly one crossing and names it — nomos may not reach a `kwb-` prefix, enforced by Test_No_Crate_May_Name_The_Sibling_Knowledge_Workbench with an empty allowlist — and that direction is nomos to kwb. Nothing found in nomos's record set closes kwb to xvpe; a reader who takes 'the KWB crossing is still closed' as bearing on this item has read the direction backwards. Complicating rather than settling it: D-130 itself still reads status accepted, version 2, and still says adoption is by git reference and commit SHA into one quarantined crate and is 'never a path dependency', while nomos's own AGENTS.md records six crates naming xvpe by relative path and ten reaching one transitively. OD-PLATFORM-003's relations target AGT-006 and not D-130, and ARC-CONNECTOR-001 still says 'D-130 is untouched'. That divergence is nomos's to resolve; what belongs here is that this repository is citing the side of it that practice left behind. Completeness is a classification claim, not a feeling: it needs a denominator that says what counted as a scoped surface, a classification of every one of them, and a destination for every artifact in a retained class — otherwise it is a coverage report that cannot say what it skipped. Per D-003 each extracted requirement also carries the evidentiary level it actually reached, because implementation presence is not evidence of semantic validity. items.title: The bands table names kwb-store a content-addressed document store and names no database, while the prototype's retrieval was Postgres-native and measured
items.why: The prototype's retrieval is the most thoroughly measured thing in that tree: a vector(768) column with an HNSW cosine index (m=16, ef_construction=64), full-text as a GIN expression index over to_tsvector, ts_rank_cd scoring, and an EXPLAIN-based test asserting the plan rather than the result. Measured live at 7,914 chunks: 38 ms keyword against 1.3 ms vector (PostgresKeywordSearchTests.cs:146). That is not evidence that persistence should change, and it is not permission to port EF and Postgres either. The question this item holds is: what storage semantics did the prototype prove are required? Answer that and the mechanism — Postgres and pgvector, an XVPE abstraction over them, or something else — follows from a requirement rather than from inherited implementation. Three pieces of prototype evidence bear on it and pull in different directions. First, Infrastructure/Repositories runs three backends (in-memory, JSON, EF) behind one Expression<Func<T,bool>> interface, which is the single strongest argument ADR 0001 gives for C#. Second, that repository's own successor analysis contradicts it: KWB_database_depth_assessment topic 03 names the generic repository as what 'flattens PostgreSQL into a key-value store', says the specialized repositories are the better direction, and argues the end state needs more in the database, not less — recursive CTEs, window functions, LATERAL joins, materialized views, SKIP LOCKED, advisory locks, row versioning. Third, EfCore/Queries and EfCore/Repositories hold what was actually built against that ambition. This is held ground under D-004: the item reserves it and produces a requirement record, not a schema.
items.done_when: A record here states what storage semantics the prototype proved are required — separating what must be true of any store (durability, atomicity, temporal reads, uniqueness under a liveness expression, ranked retrieval) from what happened to be Postgres — citing the prototype measurement behind each, and says explicitly which of those requirements the bands table's current description of kwb-store does and does not cover. It names no implementation and proposes no crate.

items.title: A user's preference and a theorem would enter this repository's graph as the same kind of thing, and the corpus says that is how KWB gets contaminated
items.why: XVPE/video 6.txt §17 proposes a hierarchy of knowledge scopes — universal mathematics, physical and hardware theory, programming-language theory, domain engineering knowledge, toolchain-specific knowledge, hardware-specific evidence, XVPE experimental evidence, project-specific evidence, user preferences — with the rule that preserving scope is essential and a more general claim outranks a more specific one. §16 gives the mechanism it exists to prevent: choosing static dispatch for one scheduler is a ProjectDecision, not UniversalEngineeringKnowledge, and KWB may record the case as evidence under stated conditions (workload, target, constraints) but only accumulated evidence forms a broader conditional claim. Without a scope, an arbitrary historical choice and a proven result are the same row. This is absent from the prototype entirely and absent from this board, and it is load-bearing for the ecosystem seam in particular: ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 gives KWB long-term epistemic memory, and D-135 sends genuinely domain-neutral code to XVPE, so a KWB claim that silently carried project scope would cross both boundaries wearing the wrong label. Held ground under D-004 — it sits directly on promotion and authorization, which the reference miner is still generating requirements for.
items.done_when: A record here states whether a scope is a property of a claim, of an assertion of a claim, or of a context the claim is scoped to, and what promotion from a narrower scope to a broader one requires as evidence — or states why the question is deferred and names what would reopen it. It defines no scope enumeration: naming the levels is the easy half and the corpus already did it.

items.title: D-005 decided the board adopts nomos-ledger's schema, and until the migration lands no item on this board can be finished at all
items.why: D-005 is a decision and changes nothing by itself. Two items — KWB-7 and KWB-9 — are parked in Claimed with their work delivered because AGENTS.md forbids hand-editing an item to Done and nothing exists to transition them otherwise, and every other item on this board would reach the same wall on completion. This item is the migration that makes AGENTS.md's own loop completable for the first time. Measured 2026-09-12 against a throwaway copy, detail in docs/corpus/nomos-as-precedent.md: the whole gap is kind and origin per item drawn from nomos's closed sets (Capability|Decision|Validation|Correction|Cleanup, Required|Proposed, capitalized — the refusal names the set), schema_version 1 against 5, and a Claim that is {holder, acquired_at, lease_expires_at} with integer epoch timestamps rather than the prose note KWB-7 and KWB-9 currently carry, so that prose moves into each item's why. Two further facts the probe established. First, `nomos work finish` refuses at exit 4 when .github/workflows/gate.yml cannot be read, on the grounds that an item finished against a check weaker than the gate is the defect the refusal exists to prevent — this repository has no CI at all, so the workflow is a precondition of the decision working and not an extra. Second, the probe's `work list` reported KWB-9 as lapsed rather than claimed, which is the lease behaviour whose absence caused this board's deadlock; it arrives with the schema at no extra cost. Nothing in the build graph changes: no Cargo.toml gains an edge, no crate names nomos- or xvpe-, and tests/contract's bands table is untouched.
items.done_when: work/ledger.json is at schema_version 5 with kind and origin on every item and no hand-written claim shape; .github/workflows/gate.yml exists and runs at least cargo test --workspace and a lint step; `nomos work validate` run from this repository's root exits 0 and reports that the build understands the schema; and `nomos work finish` has been used to transition KWB-7 and KWB-9, so the first items closed on this board are closed through the tool rather than by hand. The prose currently held in KWB-7's and KWB-9's claim objects survives the migration in their why fields; losing it is a failure of this item, not a detail of the format.

items.title: Steps 7 and 8 of the product loop are what make it a loop, and nothing in the prototype or on this board owns either
items.why: The design corpus states KWB's central product loop in ten steps (topic 054 in the game plan): a passage is ingested, claims are extracted, claims are connected to normalized concepts, relation assertions are proposed, evidence and context are attached, existing assertions are corroborated or challenged, derived connections are recomputed, stale syntheses are invalidated, users inspect why a connection exists, and users compare current and historical interpretations. Measured against the prototype 2026-09-12, detail in docs/corpus/what-kwb-is-for.md: steps 1-4 and 6 are substantially built, and steps 7 and 8 are not partial but zero. `DerivationDependency` 0 files, `Staleness` 0 files, `Invalidate` 0 files, `GraphVersion` 0 files. DerivationLedger looks like it should cover them and does not: DerivationRecord is {RunId, ChunkId, NodeId, ModelVersion, PromptHash, ResponseHash, Rationale, Outcome}, which records that a node came from a chunk via a model. That is a provenance record, not a dependency edge — nothing anywhere says this synthesis depends on these claims, so a changed claim invalidates it. Without recompute-and-invalidate, steps 1-6 are a pipeline that runs once rather than a loop, which is the prototype's actual condition: it compiled a corpus and then had no mechanism to notice the corpus changing underneath it. Four independent readings land here. The nine operations (415) put `revise` among the absent. The prototype's own ROADMAP lists thirteen gaps verified absent from its source tree and `DerivationDependency` and staleness propagation are first. The corpus's own sequencing (topic 053) makes 'add derivation dependencies and staleness' its Phase 3. And essay.txt, reviewing the prototype independently, groups derivation dependencies with graph snapshots, identity transitions, destructive-operation preview, producer identity and coverage-on-answers as the most important group because 'those increase reliability of everything built afterward'. This item is unusual on this board in one respect worth stating: it is NOT on D-004's held list. The reference miner is generating requirements for the evidence ontology, admission, coverage and the confidence model — it is not generating any for dependency tracking and invalidation, which is a mechanical question about what depends on what. So this is specifiable now, while steps 5 and 10 are not. NOT CLAIMABLE ON ARRIVAL, and the reason is worth keeping rather than fixing: this item's territory is docs/records and docs/corpus, which is exactly what it must write, and both are held by KWB-7 and KWB-9 — two items whose work is finished and which are parked in Claimed because nothing can transition them to Done. Narrowing this item's territory would be drawing it against what is free rather than against what the change must edit, which is the authoring mistake OD-LEDGER-001 measures. So it stays correct and blocked. This is the third territory collision on this board in one session and the first one that blocks real design work rather than bookkeeping; under the lease model D-005 adopted, both holders would have lapsed and released automatically. KWB-13 is what unblocks this.
items.done_when: A record here states what a derivation dependency must relate and what an invalidation must guarantee, derived from the failure it prevents rather than from the prototype's shape — including, at minimum: what a derived artifact declares it was derived FROM (not merely by which run and model, which is all DerivationRecord captures), what happens to a derived artifact when one of its inputs changes versus when one is retracted, whether invalidation marks or deletes (D17 answers this and the record must show its work), and how a consumer distinguishes a stale artifact from a current one without having to remember to ask. The record names which of the prototype's five recorded incidents its rules answer, and states explicitly what it does NOT cover — versioning and snapshots (loop step 10) depend on this and are not this.

items.title: kwb-model can derive an identity from normalized text and from nothing else, so the document store cannot address a document without either losing bytes or minting identity twice
items.why: KWB-2 is the first consumer of KWB-1 and does not fit through it. Derivation offers With_Text, With_Identity and With_Absent; With_Text runs Normalize, which collapses every whitespace run and strips every C0/C1 control character. That is exactly right for a claim, where a reflow is not an edit, and it is destructive for a stored document. Two documents differing only in indentation derive one identity, so the second write finds the first already present, reports success, and the second document bytes are gone. That is a D17 incident in the precise shape D17 names: a write that reports success while destroying evidence it had no basis to destroy. The alternative open to kwb-store inside its own territory is to hash bytes itself with sha2, which AGENTS.md refuses as introducing a second authority for something already governed, and which would put two derivation layouts in one workspace with nothing asserting they agree. So identity for opaque bytes is kwb-model work, discovered by KWB-2, and it is a door on the existing Derivation rather than a new scheme.
items.done_when: Derivation admits raw bytes as a participating field through one door that does not normalize them, documented where it is defined with what it does not do and why a caller must not reach for it when the field is text. The layout keeps every property KWB-1 paid for: the field name participates, the separator still cannot be forged from inside a value, and an absent field still occupies its place. Tests assert that two byte strings differing only in whitespace derive different identities, that a byte field and a text field of the same name and content do not collide, and that a value containing the separator byte cannot forge a field boundary through the bytes door. kwb-model builds and tests green, and no caller outside kwb-model is required for this item to close.

items.title: This repository has no .gitattributes, two files checked in with CRLF and the rest with LF, and a gate that will one day compare bytes
items.why: core.autocrlf is true and .gitattributes is absent, so what lands in a working tree depends on the machine that checked it out. Measured today: kwb-model content_identity.rs and tests.rs are CRLF on disk, every other source file is LF, and committing anything prints a warning per file about endings changing the next time git touches it. git diff reports none of this, because git compares normalized content, so the disagreement is invisible to exactly the tool a session would reach for. The cost is not hypothetical in a repository built this way. A gate that compares raw bytes -- a generated table, a golden file, a digest of a source tree -- fails against a checkout git calls clean, and the session that inherits it has no way to see why. This repository already derives identity from bytes, so it is more exposed to this than most.
items.done_when: A .gitattributes at the repository root declares text handling explicitly rather than leaving it to a per-machine setting, the two CRLF files are normalized so the tree is internally consistent, and the whole workspace still builds, tests and lints green afterwards. A line-ending change that silently altered a source file would be the failure this item exists to prevent, so the verification is the workspace test run and not an inspection of the diff.

items.title: The board cannot reserve a record that has not been numbered yet, so every decision item reserves the whole records directory and the board serialises
items.why: Measured across one session that closed six items. Adding an item to correct D-004 -- a correction D-004 itself mandates -- was refused because docs/records is reserved by KWB-3, which nobody is holding. Five of the items authored with a record in their done_when reserve the directory rather than a file, and add refuses any new item overlapping an open one, so while any decision item is unclosed no new decision item can be proposed at all. The refusal suggests retiring the blocking item, which inverts the situation. This is not carelessness in the authoring. The tool supports file granularity and says so, but only for a record that already exists: --amends reserves a published file, and there is no way to reserve a record identifier that has not been allocated yet. An item that will write a decision cannot name what it will write, so the only reservation available to it is the directory. That is the root cause, and it is a gap in the mechanism rather than in the items. Three smaller findings sit beside it and are cheap to state: work show advertises an item in full and prints no why, no done_when and no territory, so a session following the loop must parse work/ledger.json by hand to see the predicate it is told to run; --amends refuses the identifier a record declares for itself and accepts only the path, though the identifier is how every record in this repository cites every other; and the board reserves ground without defending it, which cost two territory slips in this session alone, both the same shape of writing first and reserving after.
items.done_when: An observation document records each finding with what was measured and the command that showed it, separates the root cause from its symptoms, and says for each whether the remedy belongs to how items are authored here or to the ledger tool this repository borrowed and took no dependency on under D-005. Where the remedy is the tool, the document states what the mechanism would have to offer rather than proposing an implementation, because that code is not this repository. It closes no finding by itself and asserts nothing about nomos, which is a sibling this repository does not govern.

Its governing rule -- observation proceeds and a decision that depends on an open input does not -- is unchanged, because nothing measured contradicts it and only the dependencies were wrong. No held subject acquires a type, schema or vocabulary here.

items.title: D-008 said the second store decision was blocked on the domain types, and KWB-3 and KWB-4 have closed
items.why: D-008 measured that the bands table names one store where the prototype evidence describes two: an immutable artifact store, which kwb-store is, and a mutable versioned graph, which nothing here has and no row names. Seven of the eight storage requirements the prototype proved -- one liveness expression, uniqueness under it, which-world reads, temporal reconstruction, contradiction refusal, the lease, ranked retrieval -- land on the second, and kwb-domain names the types without saying where they live. D-008 deliberately stopped at naming the gap and recorded that deciding it was blocked on what those types are, which is KWB-3 and KWB-4. Both have now closed, so the blocker has cleared and the decision is owed. It is also blocking work already on the board: KWB-6 requires that current-version and all-versions reads be distinct types rather than one type with a flag, which is D19-B translated into this workspace, and over a content-addressed store where every document is immutable and there is exactly one version of everything that distinction is two names for identical behaviour. Building it now would produce a gate that passes because there is nothing for it to catch, which is the defect rather than the requirement. Durability is the other half: kwb-store holds documents in memory for the length of a process, recorded by KWB-2 as a deferral to this question and not an oversight.
items.done_when: A record decides what holds the mutable versioned graph and what holds durable bytes -- whether that is one crate, two, a set of port traits, or a decision that this repository does not need mutable storage and the seven requirements are met another way. It answers against D-008s eight requirements explicitly, requirement by requirement, saying which the decision meets, which it defers and which it declines, because a storage decision that does not say that is a decision nobody can check. It names no database and no library, and where it defers it names what would settle the deferral. D-008s warning attaches: the cost of a retrieval shape is invisible to correctness tests, measured at 38 ms against 1.3 ms on byte-identical rows, so a choice made here cannot be validated by the tests passing.

items.title: D-005 deferred owning ledger code because one product used it, and KWB using it makes two
items.why: D-005 decided this repository adopts nomos-ledger schema and takes no dependency on its code, and its reasoning was explicit about why: D-135 governs where new domain-neutral code is authored, nomos-ledger is 14,008 existing lines, so ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 two-product proof governs instead, and at the time there was one product. There are now two. This repository operates its board by running that binary daily, so the condition D-005 named as deciding the question has been met by events rather than by argument. OD-LEDGER-001 measured what the current arrangement costs: an item cannot reserve a record it has not numbered, so every decision item reserves the whole records directory, and while any decision item is open no new decision item can be proposed at all. That is not a grievance about a tool, it is the predictable result of a shared mechanism having no owner who can change it -- this repository cannot fix it because D-005 correctly says the code is not ours, and Nomos has no reason to prioritise a constraint it does not feel. A work ledger is not knowledge and it is not software-engineering analysis. It is a coordination mechanism, which is exactly the shape D-135 and ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 assign to XVPE, and xvpe-event-journal is the worked precedent: it came out of the reference miner because the part that does not know what is being journalled was trapped where nothing else could reach it.
items.done_when: A record here states this repository position -- that the work ledger is a shared coordination mechanism and belongs to XVPE under D-135, that D-005 deferral condition has been met, and what this repository would consume and what it would keep. It does not decide the ecosystem question, because AGENTS.md routes that to ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 in Nomos and this repository does not restate what it does not own; it states a position and names the evidence, so the upstream decision has something measured to act on. It proposes no crate name and moves no code.

items.title: D-010 decided a scope belongs to an assertion and there is no assertion type, so claims currently have nowhere to put a source or a scope
items.why: KWB-4 built Claim and Concept, and both deliberately exclude the source and the scope from their identity -- the source so two references asserting one claim become one claim with two citations, the scope because D-010 measured that a scope in the identity would make a benchmark and a mere preference saying the same thing two rows that can never learn of each other. Both exclusions are right and both leave a hole. A claim currently records what is asserted and nothing about who asserted it, from where, or over what domain, so the citations the whole dedup mechanism exists to accumulate have nowhere to accumulate. D-010 named the missing type in as many words and said it is where a grade attaches. D-004 version 2 puts both halves of it on closed ground: the verification and provenance axis of the evidence model closed on measurement, and what a scope belongs to closed by D-010 needing no miner input at all. What stays open is the grading, which is the epistemic-strength model and is pending rather than stranded.
items.done_when: kwb-domain has an assertion type that binds a claim to the source asserting it and the scope it is asserted at, with an identity derived from all three -- so that one claim carries many assertions and two assertions of one claim by two sources are two rows that meet at the claim. It carries no confidence, grade or strength of any kind, and a test fixes that absence, because the epistemic-strength model is on D-004 held list as pending and an assertion that graded itself now would be the settable Confidence = 1.0 the prototype shipped in forty types. Tests defend the properties rather than the accessors: two sources asserting one claim produce one claim and two assertions, the same source asserting the same claim twice is one assertion, and a scope change produces a different assertion of the same claim.

items.title: kwb-platform-xvpe is reserved in the manifest and does not exist, so D-012 decision that versioned state is adopted rather than written has never been acted on and liveness has nothing to be true of
items.why: D-012 decided the mutable versioned graph is adopted from XVPE rather than built here, because xvpe-collections-persistent already ships structures whose old versions remain valid and independently queryable -- which makes D-008 which-world read and temporal reconstruction structural rather than a discipline. D-007 decided adoption is by git reference and commit SHA into a crate that quarantines it, never by path. Neither decision has been acted on, and the crate both of them name is a comment in the workspace manifest. That matters more than an unbuilt crate usually would, because two accepted records rest on a mechanism nobody had exercised until it was probed today: a SHA-pinned git dependency on an XVPE workspace member resolves and compiles in 37 seconds, measured against a7eee3c6e on origin/dev. The second half is the consumer. D-008 first requirement is that liveness is one expression, and it is the one this repository is most likely to violate by accident -- the prototype index enforced half the rule for three weeks and nothing failed, because a half-rule is a weaker constraint and weaker constraints raise no errors. A liveness expression needs versioned concept state to be true of, and there is none.
items.done_when: kwb-platform-xvpe exists at band 1p, adopts the persistent map by git reference and commit SHA with no path edge anywhere, and has a row in the bands table so tests/contract passes both directions. kwb-domain has versioned concept state built on it, carrying a standing for each concept and exactly one liveness expression, with a current-concepts read and an every-version read that are different types rather than one type with a flag. Tests defend the properties: there is one liveness expression and no second copy of the rule, a superseded concept is absent from the current read and present in the every-version read, publishing a version leaves the previous version valid and queryable, and the two reads cannot be confused for one another by forgetting anything.

items.title: Admission hands back concepts and claims, the graph holds concepts, and nothing connects them
items.why: KWB-5 built the pipeline and KWB-24 built versioned state, and between them there is nothing. Admit returns its concepts and claims to its caller deliberately -- D19 forbids enqueueing for a consumer that does not exist, and at the time D-008 had measured that the store claims belong in had no crate. D-012 answered that and KWB-24 built it, so the consumer now exists and the deliberate gap has become an ordinary one. Left as it is, this repository has an ingestion pipeline whose output reaches nothing and a graph nothing fills: complete, tested code connected to no other code, which is the defect this family of repositories produces most often. The graph is also concept-only. Claims and assertions are versioned by the same mechanism or they are not versioned at all, and a claim that cannot be closed cannot be corrected -- while a concept can. That asymmetry is not a decision anybody made.
items.done_when: Admission writes its concepts and claims into versioned state through one call, and returns the new graph value rather than mutating one -- so the caller still holds what it had, which is what makes the previous version a thing that was kept. The graph holds claims and assertions as well as concepts, under one liveness rule and still with exactly one definition of it. Tests defend the connection rather than the pieces: what admission reports as admitted is what the resulting graph holds, a re-admitted source adds no duplicate concept, and a claim whose concept is closed is reachable through the all-versions read and not through the current one -- because a claim about a retired concept is not a current claim, and saying so is the point of having one liveness rule rather than two.

items.title: Every piece of the pipeline is tested and nothing has ever run it, because kwb-cli is an empty main
items.why: kwb-store, kwb-domain and kwb-ingest are built and green, and the only thing that has ever exercised them together is a test harness. The bands table names kwb-cli the composition root and it is a main that does nothing. A pipeline that has never run outside its own tests is the shape this family of repositories keeps producing -- and the repository has spent this session finding instances of it in the prototype and in its own dependencies, so leaving one here would be poor form. There is a second reason and it is concrete. D-012 deferred durability and named the condition precisely: it is settled by an item that decides where durable bytes land, which needs a consumer that actually loses something when the process ends, and nothing here has one because nothing here runs for longer than a test. A composition root is exactly that consumer. Building it does not decide durability and must not; it creates the thing whose absence made the question unanswerable.
items.done_when: kwb-cli admits a real file through the real pipeline and reports what happened, using the same Coverage vocabulary the library does rather than a second one -- so a run that examined nothing says unmet and a run that examined and found nothing says barren, and the two are distinguishable at the command line as well as in the types. It invents no extractor and pretends to no model: what a passage asserts is supplied by the caller, and the help says so plainly rather than leaving a reader to infer that the interesting half is missing. A wrong command line exits differently from a run that failed. The workspace builds, tests and lints green, and the composition root names no backend the library does not already have.

items.title: D-012 deferred durability and named the condition that would settle it, and KWB-26 built that condition
items.why: D-012 answered seven of D-008 eight storage requirements and left durability, saying explicitly that it is a backend rather than a schema and that settling it needs a consumer which actually loses something when the process ends -- and that nothing here had one, because nothing ran longer than a test. KWB-26 is that consumer: kwb admit reads a file, admits it, prints what happened and exits, and everything it built is gone. The condition D-012 named has been met by building the thing whose absence made the question unanswerable, which is the sequence D-012 asked for rather than an argument for skipping it. There is a measurement to make first and it is cheap, so the decision should not be taken without it: the two things that are lost are not lost in the same way, and a single durability answer covering both would be answering two questions with one.
items.done_when: A record states what must survive a process and why, separately for the content-addressed documents and for the versioned graph, with the reproducibility of each measured rather than assumed. It says what the platform port must offer for each, naming no library and no file format beyond what the measurement forces. Where it defers, it names the condition. D-012 warning attaches and is repeated in it: a retrieval shape cost is invisible to correctness tests, measured at 38 ms against 1.3 ms on byte-identical rows, so a choice made here cannot be validated by the tests passing.

items.title: D-014 decided documents go to content-addressed files and kwb-platform has no traits at all
items.why: D-014 answered the document half of durability completely -- one file per address, no index, no overwrite, writes atomic by temp-then-rename -- and named exactly what a port must offer to serve it. kwb-platform is a doc comment with no traits, and kwb-platform-std is a doc comment with no implementations, so the decision has nothing to be implemented against. kwb admit still loses every byte it writes. The atomicity requirement is the part that must not be got wrong and the reason to do this carefully rather than quickly: a half-written file under a content address is the one way this store can lie, because the address promises the bytes and nothing downstream re-hashes what it reads, so a truncated file is a silent corruption rather than a loud failure.
items.done_when: kwb-platform declares a filesystem port sufficient for a content-addressed store and nothing wider, kwb-platform-std implements it over the standard library, and kwb-store can be constructed over one so that writes land on disk and survive the process. The one-write-door property is unchanged and its test still passes: persistence is reached through the existing door, never beside it. A write is atomic -- a reader never sees a partial file under a complete address -- and a test demonstrates it rather than the code asserting it. An in-memory store still works with no backing at all, because a test suite that needed a filesystem to test a type would be testing the filesystem.

items.title: Concept and Claim store text as given while their identity is derived from it normalized, so a value can disagree with its own address
items.why: Measured 2026-09-12. Concept::Named("a  b") and Concept::Named("a b") derive the same identity -- correctly, because a reflow is not an edit -- and Canonical_Name returns "a  b" and "a b". The identity says one concept and the accessor says two different things. Claim::Text is the same. Assertion::Source and Scope::Name already store the normalized form, so two of the four text-carrying types normalize what they keep and two do not, and nothing decided that. Two concrete costs. Whichever spelling is published first wins in a map, so what a reader gets back depends on insertion order rather than on content -- in a repository whose premise is that content decides everything. And it blocks the durability record cleanly: replaying a publication would store one spelling and the replayed graph could differ textually from the live one while being identically addressed, which is a reproducibility defect in exactly the property this repository rests on. The identity has already decided that the difference is not part of what the thing is; the stored value should agree with it.
items.done_when: Concept and Claim keep the normalized form of their text, so an accessor never disagrees with the identity derived from the same input, and all four text-carrying types agree about what they keep. Tests fix the property rather than the spelling: two spellings that derive one identity render one text, and a claim and a concept that differ in case still differ, because case is significant and normalization does not fold it. The whole workspace still builds, tests and lints green, which is also the check that nothing depended on the unnormalized form.

items.title: D-014 decided the graph becomes durable by replaying what was published and nothing records a publication
items.why: kwb admit keeps its bytes since KWB-31 and forgets everything it learned. D-014 decided the shape -- an append-only record of publications, replayed to reconstruct, with the temporal read falling out as a prefix rather than needing a second mechanism -- and named what a port must offer: append a record, read the records in order. Neither the port nor the record exists. KWB-32 makes this cleanly possible for a reason worth stating: every text a domain type keeps is now normalized, and Normalize strips every control character, so no field can contain a separator or a newline. A separator-framed record is therefore unambiguous because the domain guarantees it, not because an encoder escapes it -- the same guarantee KWB-1 established for identity derivation, used a second time. That removes the serialization-library decision D-014 said nothing forced.
items.done_when: kwb-platform declares a record-log port and kwb-platform-std implements it over a file, one record per line. kwb-domain encodes a publication and replays a sequence of them into a graph, and a graph replayed from its own publications equals the graph that produced them -- asserted by comparing what both hold rather than by trusting the encoder. A record whose value would derive a different address than the record names is refused rather than admitted, because a replayed graph that silently differed from the one recorded would break the property everything here rests on. A value containing a separator cannot forge a field boundary, and there is a test that would fail if the domain stopped normalizing.

items.title: A backed store decides Stored or AlreadyPresent from memory alone, so every process reports storing what it already durably held
items.why: Measured. Write a document to a backed store, drop the store, open another over the same directory and write the same document: the receipt says Stored and Was_Stored returns true, for bytes that were already on disk and which Put correctly skipped. The receipt means this write is what put the bytes there and it is false. That is precisely the lie Written and Admission were built to prevent -- D19, a success value produced on a path that did no work -- and KWB-30 reintroduced it by adding a durable backing while leaving the decision keyed on the in-memory map. D-008 recorded content-addressed idempotence as stronger than an idempotency key because a key can be forgotten and content cannot; across processes that is currently untrue, and a caller counting admissions over-reports by exactly the number of documents it already had. Worth saying plainly: this was introduced by me, today, in the crate whose one job is not lying about writes, and it was found by probing my own work rather than by any test failing.
items.done_when: A backed store decides its admission from what it actually holds, memory or medium, so re-admitting a durably held document reports AlreadyPresent and Was_Stored is false. An unbacked store is unchanged. A failure to ask the medium refuses the write rather than guessing, because guessing would put the lie back with an extra step. Tests cover the case a process boundary creates -- a store opened over a directory another store wrote -- since that is the only place this defect lives and no single-process test would have caught it.

items.title: Nothing can close a concept, so a merge loser is a state only a test has ever produced, and a supersede records no evidence authorising it
items.why: Two findings from the same sweep that found KWB-36. Standing has three variants and production constructs only Asserted -- Retired and Superseded appear solely in the encode and decode halves of replay, which means the closing path can only ever read records nothing writes. Merge_Losers, the question D19-B says merge-audit needed and asked of the wrong world, can therefore only ever answer about an empty set, and the whole current-versus-historical distinction this repository has spent several records justifying has nothing to distinguish. And the second, which is the sharper one: Standing::Superseded carries its successor and nothing else. D17 is that destruction requires evidence, and the question it demands be answerable before a delete, deprecate, supersede or overwrite is "what belief authorises this, and what would falsify it". A supersede that records the successor and not the reason cannot answer it. The prototype was better here -- it kept a ConceptMerge log its own merge-audit re-read -- and this repository, which cites that incident in four records, currently has no place to put the answer.
items.done_when: Closing a concept records what authorised it. A supersede names its successor and the belief behind it, a retirement names its reason, and neither is constructible without one -- so the question D17 demands be answerable is answerable by construction rather than by whoever remembers to write it down. The reason survives a record and a replay. The command line can retire and supersede, so the closing path is reachable outside a test and a merge loser is a state the product can actually produce. Superseding something into itself is refused, and so is superseding into a concept the graph does not hold, because both are merges whose successor cannot be resolved and D17 is about not destroying on a belief nobody checked.

items.title: Record relations are declared one way, so three records still assert things this repository stopped doing and a reader of them cannot find the correction
items.why: Measured: of 27 relations declared in record frontmatter, 24 have no counterpart in the record they point at. Only three are discoverable from both ends, and those three only because D-004 amendment happened to name them. So the record graph is almost entirely backward-linked, and a reader of an older record cannot reach the newer one that answered or amended it. That is not theoretical. D-008 says durability in any form is uncovered because kwb-store holds documents in memory for the length of a process; KWB-30 made it durable. D-012 says the same sentence about documents and adds that a persistent structure holds versions the same way; KWB-33 and KWB-34 record and replay them. D-013 says the evidence vocabulary lives in the reference miner reachable by nothing; it was extracted to xvpe-evidence. Each correction exists and none is reachable from where the false statement is. AGENTS.md says records are canonical and routes every why question to them, so a canonical record asserting something the code stopped doing is the stale-premise defect this session has now found five times in code, occurring one level up in the documents that are supposed to be the fix for it.
items.done_when: Every relation a record declares is discoverable from both ends, and a check asserts it rather than a convention requiring it -- so a record that answers an earlier one cannot be written without the earlier one gaining a way to reach it. The three false statements are corrected where they stand, by amendment rather than rewriting, because what a record said and when it stopped being true is the thing a reader needs and a silent edit destroys it. The check fails if a relation is added in one direction only, verified by adding one.

items.title: Two crates advertise capabilities they do not have, and one contradicts its own source file
items.why: Found by sweeping the authorities the way KWB-38 swept the records. kwb-platform is described in its manifest and in the README bands table as offering port traits for clock, filesystem, lock and process. It exports two traits, ContentStoreStrategy and RecordLogStrategy, and neither is in that list, and its own lib.rs says in as many words that the clock, lock and process ports are not here yet. One fact in three places, two of them agreeing with each other and both disagreeing with the code. kwb-retrieval advertises keyword, semantic, hybrid and neighbourhood queries; semantic and hybrid do not exist, its own lib.rs says semantic is absent and deliberately not stubbed, and D-004 holds the ground it would need. So a crate is advertising the one capability this repository has explicitly refused to fake. The underlying mistake is the same in both: a description that inventories what a crate has goes stale every time the crate changes, while a description that says what a crate is for cannot. The bands table is asserted by tests/contract for crate names and not for descriptions, so the descriptions have been drifting unwatched since the first commit.
items.done_when: Neither crate advertises a capability it does not have. Both descriptions say what the crate is for rather than listing what it contains, because an inventory in a description is a copy of the source that drifts and a charter is not -- and the fix for a fact restated in three places is to stop restating it, not to check it harder. The bands table and the manifests agree, and a check asserts that, so the remaining drift mode between the two places that must still each carry a description is closed rather than left to notice. The check fails if one is edited without the other, verified by editing one.

items.why: Every consumer handles it -- Name, Findings, Was_Run and Is_Evidence_Of_Absence all have an arm for it, and a test exercises it -- and nothing in this repository constructs one. items.title: The corpus prescribes how three incidents should be encoded here, all three were encoded differently, and nothing says which is right
items.why: The surveys are measurements of the prototype and cannot go stale, but each incident ends with a What would encode it here section, and those are prescriptions about code that did not exist when they were written and does now. D17 says the coverage type should have its unknown value as its default. Coverage has no Default at all, deliberately, because D20 states deriving a status as the primary rule and ordering the zero value only as the fallback if it must be assigned -- Of_Run derives, so the fallback is moot and the implementation took the stronger of the two. The corpus states the fallback as though it were the requirement, so it now under-describes what was built and a reader comparing them cannot tell an improvement from a miss. D19 prescribes a job kind that cannot be enqueued without a registered handler, failing that a status enum whose unhandled arm retains; admission has no queue at all, which is stronger and is not what the prescription describes. And D19-B says two distinct read types and liveness as one expression with a test that no second copy exists, owned by KWB-6 -- both were built under KWB-24, so the routing points at an item that did not do it. Three prescriptions, three divergences, none recorded, in the documents the records cite as evidence.
items.done_when: Each of the three prescriptions says what was actually built and why it differs, where it differs -- as an amendment beside the prescription rather than a rewrite of it, because what the survey recommended before the code existed is the thing a reader is comparing against and editing it away destroys the comparison. Where the implementation took a stronger rule than the prescription named, the record says so and names the rule; where the ownership moved to another item, it names that item. No measurement of the prototype is touched, because none of them has stopped being true.

items.title: The guards detect defects with parsers nothing has ever shown can detect anything, and one parser exists twice with two different bodies
items.why: A clean audit pass produced this. All eleven guards were re-broken and all eleven caught their defect, so nothing they guard is wrong. What the pass exposed is one level up. Every guard works by scanning source text with a small parser -- Mutating_Public_Methods, Liveness_Definitions, Declared_Relations, the routing and description readers -- and every one of those parsers is only ever run against the real tree, which passes. A parser that always returned empty would pass identically. The eleven verifications this session did were done by hand, mutating real files and restoring them, which is neither repeatable nor something the suite does, so a detector that silently stopped detecting would look exactly like a green test. That is the defect class this audit exists for, applied to the audit itself. Separately, Mutating_Public_Methods exists in kwb-store and in kwb-retrieval with different bodies -- one fact copied and drifted, which is the other class, and it means the two crates are guarded by two detectors nobody has compared.
items.done_when: Each source-scanning detector is exercised against input that should trip it and input that should not, so a detector that stopped detecting fails the suite rather than passing it quietly. The inputs are synthetic strings, not the real tree and not a mutation of it: a test that edits source to prove a point can leave a tree broken when it fails, and this repository has enough respect for that failure mode to not introduce it. The two copies of the mutating-method detector are both covered by the same cases, so drift between them becomes a failure rather than something nobody compares -- and whether to extract them into one is recorded either way, because twenty duplicated lines and a new shared crate are both real costs and the choice should be visible.

items.why: The first line of README.md describes KWB in the present tense -- it ingests references and builds a durable graph of the concepts they teach, deduplicated across sources by content-derived identity. items.title: Admission takes a list of extractions rather than an extractor, so the seam the admission rule requires does not exist
items.why: The README first line says KWB ingests references and builds a graph of the concepts they teach. It cannot: nothing reads a document and decides what it says, and a person types the claims through --says. The obvious next step is an extractor, and the corpus own admission rule says where it may not go. Its second test is whether a feature would still make sense if the model were replaced by a perfect human annotator -- yes means it is KWB, no means it is an AI capability KWB happens to use. Extraction as a step passes that test, because a person reading a passage and writing down what it asserts is a real step. Extraction by a model fails it. So the step belongs here and the model-backed implementation does not, and building one inside kwb-ingest would put an AI capability inside the knowledge engine, which is the one thing the rule exists to prevent. There is a second reason to do this before any extractor exists rather than after. kwb admit --says is already an implementation of that port -- it is literally the perfect human annotator the rule describes -- and it is unnamed, so the seam is being used without being declared. Declaring it costs almost nothing now and is a refactor of every caller later.
items.done_when: kwb-ingest declares what an extractor is, in its own vocabulary rather than a platform one, because the port deals in concepts and claims where kwb-platform ports deal in bytes. Admit takes an extractor rather than a prepared list, so the pipeline asks for what a passage says instead of being handed it. The stated-extractions implementation is named as what it is -- a person supplying the claims, the case the admission rule calls a perfect human annotator -- and the command line uses it, so the port has a real implementation from the moment it exists rather than waiting for a model. An extractor that fails is a run that could not read its source, which is not the same as a source that says nothing, and the two are distinguishable in what admission reports. No model, no provider, no xvpe dependency is added here.

Declined.reason: Superseded by KWB-47, which carries the owner specification of the same boundary.

abandoned.reason: Superseded before any work was done. The owner supplied a fuller specification of the extraction boundary the same hour: the output is source-local and deliberately not a Knowledge IR, carries source location, extraction protocol and model lineage, distinguishes text-ready from requires-visual-reading rather than pretending v1 solves multimodality, and must not import the reference miner identity semantics. This item done_when named none of that. Re-authored as KWB-47.

items.title: KWB has no extraction contract, so the first extractor would have to invent one and would invent the wrong one
items.why: The README first line says KWB ingests references; it cannot, because a person types the claims through --says. The extractor is the next major development item, and the contract it lands against decides whether the front end stays a front end. Three ways it goes wrong, each named by the owner and each already visible in this repository history. It becomes the reference miner ingestion architecture, when the miner is producing requirements and experiments and deliberately addresses source observations differently -- D-004 version 2 records that the miner finding identity absorbs the source path, the exact inverse of D-002, so importing its semantics would destroy the two-books-one-claim mechanism everything here was built for. It becomes the Knowledge IR by shipping first, when that subject is stranded and D-009 says so -- a local representation that happened to arrive cannot be allowed to become the canonical one by default. Or it lets a model write KWB entities, when the corpus admission rule second test says a feature that stops making sense with a perfect human annotator is an AI capability KWB happens to use rather than KWB. Extraction as a step passes that test; extraction by a model does not. And --says is already an implementation of the port, the literal perfect human annotator, being used without being declared.
items.done_when: kwb-ingest declares what an extractor offers and what it may not do. The output is source-local and named so it cannot be mistaken for a canonical intermediate representation: it carries the source, where in the source, the proposed claims, the protocol that produced them and the lineage of whatever produced them, and the word proposed is load-bearing -- nothing it returns is a KWB entity and it mints no identity, because identity is derived from content here and an extractor that minted one would be a second authority for the thing D-002 owns. Text-ready and requires-visual-reading are distinguishable, and a source needing visual reading is refused by a text extractor rather than silently returning nothing, because that is the difference between cannot-read and read-and-found-nothing. An extractor that fails is reported as a prerequisite unmet and never as barrenness, which Coverage already distinguishes and a test fixes. Admit takes an extractor rather than a prepared list, and the stated-extractions implementation is named as the human annotator it is and used by the command line, so the port ships with a real implementation. No model, no provider and no XVPE dependency is added by this item.

items.why: AGENTS.md routes 'What does KWB own versus Nomos, XVPE, or repository tooling?' to nomos ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 and says this repository does not restate it, which is right. ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 version 4 adopts D-122 and quotes it: a shared mechanism moves to XVPE only after two products have demonstrated materially identical domain-neutral semantics. D-135 narrows that -- D-122's proof gate governs only code that started product-specific, and code designed for shared use is proposed in XVPE the first time it is written. D-135 names this repository by name as one of the two products the narrowing is for. Nothing links the two: D-135 declares relates-to ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 and ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 does not mention D-135, so the relation is reachable from one side only, which is the exact defect KWB-38 fixed inside this repository and could not fix across the boundary. The route states that D-135 is the later and narrowing record so a reader cannot take the quoted D-122 gate as the whole rule. No record content is restated here beyond what the route needs to send a reader to the right one, because not restating is what makes this routing table correct. items.title: A stated scope that normalizes to nothing is recorded as an unstated scope, so a source that said how far it reached is recorded as having said nothing
items.why: D-010 decided that an unstated scope stays distinguishable from every stated one, because a source that did not say how far it meant has not said the narrowest thing. Scope::Named normalizes its input and an unstated scope is Scope::Named of the empty string, so the two are the same value and the distinction is carried by a magic value every caller has to know. Measured on 2026-09-12 against a rebuilt binary: kwb admit --scope '   ' and kwb admit with no --scope at all write byte-identical assertion records, both ending in an empty trailing field. A person who typed a scope and had it swallowed is told nothing, and the record says they said nothing, which is the exact reading D-010 exists to prevent -- arriving through the constructor rather than through a default. kwb-store already refuses this shape one crate down: a zero-byte document is StoreError::Vacuous because a document indistinguishable from a failed read is not something to record having admitted. A blank scope is indistinguishable from an unstated one and is admitted. Scope has the query Is_Unstated and no constructor for the thing it queries, so three callers spell Scope::Named of the empty string to mean it.
items.done_when: An unstated scope has its own constructor and is not spelled as a named scope of empty text. Scope::Named refuses text that normalizes to nothing rather than returning the unstated scope, so the silent swallow is unreachable rather than guarded at one caller -- the shape kwb-store already uses for a vacuous document, and the shape Stated::Of uses for a reader who stated nothing. kwb-cli refuses --scope with blank text and says so, rather than accepting it and recording an unstated scope. A test fails if a blank scope ever again produces the same record as an absent one, and it compares the records rather than the types, because the types agreeing is what hid this. Replay still reads an empty trailing field as unstated, because existing logs carry it and the record format is not what is wrong here.

items.title: Four string literals lost their line continuations to a scripted edit, and one of them is an error a person reads
items.why: A Rust string literal continued with a trailing backslash strips the newline and the following indentation. Python's triple-quoted strings use the same syntax, so a backslash written inside a python heredoc is consumed by python, which removes the backslash and the newline and keeps the indentation. The result compiles, lints clean and passes tests; it is only visible when the string is printed. Measured on 2026-09-12 after it reached actual CLI output in kwb-ingest and was fixed there. A sweep found five more: one in kwb-domain, fixed under KWB-50 which held that territory, and four here -- three assert messages in kwb-model tests and one in kwb-store's StoreError, which is not a test message but text a person sees when a write is refused. The tell is a run of spaces inside a literal; doc-comment alignment tables are the only legitimate hits.
items.done_when: The four literals read as written, with their continuations restored so no run of spaces survives inside a literal. The StoreError one is checked by printing it rather than by reading the source, because reading the source is what missed it four times. No wording changes beyond restoring the break, since the damage is mechanical and a rewrite would hide which text was affected.

items.title: The guard for an eaten line continuation covers one type, and the damage is a property of every string literal in the workspace
items.why: KWB-51 restored four literals whose continuations were eaten by a scripted edit and guarded StoreError by rendering it. That closes one type. The defect is not a property of StoreError: it is what happens to any Rust literal continued with a trailing backslash when the edit that writes it is itself written in a language whose strings continue the same way. Five literals were damaged across four crates in one session, one reached actual CLI output, and one survived four readings of the source because a reader's eye reconstructs the sentence. A per-type render test cannot cover the class -- ExtractionRefused, ReplayError, IdentityError and StorageError all reach a person through Display, and every assert message reaches whoever is reading a failure. KWB-44 established that a source-scanning guard here is held to showing it detects what it claims to, and this is the same shape as one_door and tool_surface.
items.done_when: A guard in tests/contract fails on a string literal anywhere under crates/ whose value carries a run of spaces in the middle of a sentence. It reconstructs the literal's value first -- removing a backslash-newline and the indentation that follows, which is what Rust itself does -- so a correctly continued literal is not flagged, and that is the property the detector is shown to have rather than asserted to have. It does not flag an aligned column in a printed table, a leading indent in a usage line, or a literal that is itself whitespace, and each of those exemptions is demonstrated by a case in the test rather than described. It is shown to detect a real instance, by reconstructing one of the five and asserting the detector finds it, because a scanner that finds nothing passes on a repository it cannot read.

items.title: Admission carries a reading's location and lineage to the door and drops both, and the type that exists to make provenance explicit says in its own documentation that it does not
items.why: KWB-47 declared ProposedReading carrying the source it read, where in it, what it proposes, and the protocol and reader that produced them. Admit consults exactly one of those four. Measured: nothing outside the seam's own tests reads Location or Lineage, and Assertion::By takes a source, a claim and a scope, so both are constructed, handed to Admit and discarded. The stated invariant that every admitted claim identifies its source occurrence and extraction protocol is therefore unmet, and Stated's documentation says the opposite in as many words -- 'now the record says which person and under what protocol' -- which is false of every record this repository writes. That is the defect this session has closed five times in other people's work, written by me, in the doc comment of the type whose whole purpose is making provenance explicit. Separately, Admit ignores the source the reading says it read and cites the document it was given instead, so a reader returning a reading about a different document has its proposals silently attributed to this one. The citation resolving to the exact bytes a claim was read out of is the strongest thing this repository claims, and nothing checks that the reader agreed about which bytes those were.
items.done_when: Admit refuses a reading whose source is not the document it was handed, as a reader that did not answer usably, so proposals cannot be attributed to a document the reader did not read. A test builds a reader that returns a reading about another document and fixes that it is refused rather than cited. The documentation says what is true: a reading carries its location and lineage to the seam and no further, what that leaves unmet, and which item owns the question. No location or lineage is added to Assertion here, because whether they belong on it and what that does to its identity is a decision and not a correction -- an assertion whose identity absorbed the protocol would make a re-read under a new prompt a second citation, and one that carried them without identifying by them would let a value disagree with itself, which KWB-32 has already fixed once.
