items.title: Two subjects D-004 calls stranded have had their stated unstranding conditions shipped, and the guard built for exactly this rot deliberately cannot see them
items.why:
D-004 v2 sorts held subjects into four states and says a stranded entry is not progressing. Three entries are stranded. KWB-62 corrected one -- the canonical Knowledge IR -- and built Test_Every_Condition_A_Record_Calls_Met_Should_Be_Met_On_The_Board so the list would stop rotting. That guard reads only a line beginning `**Condition met:**`, and its own doc comment says why: the other condition-like passages are not conditions, and a guard that is wrong half the time is switched off. That reasoning is right, and it leaves the other two entries uncovered, because their conditions are not board items at all. Both are written `*Unstranded by:*` and both name a change to xvpe.

Both changes have landed. Measured against xvpe `dev` `7ec036c52`, committed and pushed:

Cross-source corroboration. D-004 says it is unstranded by the miner acquiring a second, source-excluding claim identity, and that this is a change to the instrument rather than a longer run of it. `xvpe-corpus-ledger` ships `ClaimAssertion::Of(assertion)`, which folds in the assertion and nothing else; its doc comment argues the case in this record's own terms and names `SourceClaimIdentity` as the contrast it is built against. `ClaimLedger` carries `Support_For`, `Corroborated`, `Novel` and `Restatements` -- the support count and the falling-rate measurement D-004 says are unmeasurable while every claim is unique by construction. `xvpe-brainstorm-synthesizer/src/main.rs:1122` reads `Corroborated()` in the live binary, not a test.

Coverage and exhaustion. D-004 says it is unstranded by a coverage ledger that is read rather than another sweep, and that no `coverage`, `resume` or `redundant` symbol exists in either product. `CorpusLedger` ships `Has_Ever_Seen`, which is the nobody-looked versus looked-and-found-nothing distinction by name, with `Settlement_Of`, `UnitSettlement` and `SettlementCounts` partitioning units into answered, unanswerable and work-remaining. `xvpe-reference-miner/src/main.rs:1060` reads `Settlement_Of` in the live binary, and `xvpe-mining-memory` carries resume with tests over it. Both products depend on both crates.

So the stranded category is empty, and the amendment that predicted this rot by name is the thing that rotted. It measured at `a7eee3c6e`; `kwb-platform-xvpe` pins `8ff98a8fd`; the two crates landed at `7ec036c52`. The instrument moved twice and the pin moved once, and nothing here noticed either.

This is a re-sort, which D-004 authorises in its own words -- revised when the miner's relevant experiments close, by moving entries from the second list to the first -- and it is not a decision about any held subject. Semantic reconciliation is untouched by every measurement above, so this does not reach KWB-82.
items.done_when: D-004 is at version 3 and nothing it calls stranded is stranded. Both entries move to Pending rather than to safe-to-proceed, because the instrument can now answer these questions and has not yet been run at scale to produce the answers, and the amendment states which of those two things it is claiming for each. Every claim names the xvpe SHA it was measured at, since the last amendment's did not survive the pin moving. The amendment also states what the KWB-62 guard does not cover and why, so that the next reader is not told this list is machine-checked when the half of it that just rotted cannot be. It does not move semantic reconciliation, which no measurement here touches, and it does not weaken the rule the record exists for.

items.title: The manifest names four XVPE crates and this workspace compiles nine, and both surprises this repository has had came from the five it does not name
items.why:
`D-007` adopts XVPE by git reference and commit SHA into a crate that exists to quarantine it. The manifest names four: `xvpe-collections-persistent`, `xvpe-clock`, `xvpe-corpus-text`, `xvpe-ai-inference`. `Cargo.lock` resolves nine -- those four plus `xvpe-collections-handle`, `xvpe-collections-map`, `xvpe-collections-sequence`, `xvpe-json-text` and `xvpe-primitives`. The five are named nowhere in this repository.

The manifest states its own rule beside the pin: *Bumping the `rev` is a decision, not maintenance. What changed between two commits of another repository is exactly what a pinned dependency exists to make visible.* The pin moved from `a7eee3c6e361371b269217201233a2e7d7e36122` to `8ff98a8fd` at `KWB-72`, whose subject was D-014's last deferral, and nothing recorded what the move changed. No record mentions `8ff98a8fd` at all; `OD-GATE-001` does, to say the gate cannot fetch it.

Measured between the two commits: the four named crates did not change. `xvpe-json-text` did -- two consts widened to `pub(crate)`, and an additive method on `JsonRecordReader` with tests. That is behaviourally inert for this workspace, and it is luck rather than a finding, because nothing here established it then and nothing has since. It is also worth saying the first probe run for this was wrong: a per-crate `git diff --stat` pathspec reported `xvpe-json-text` unchanged while the full diff showed it changed, and the crate had moved directories. The instrument was wrong before the conclusion was.

This is the second time an unnamed crate has decided something here. `KWB-90` measured the build floor at 1.87 and traced it to `integer_sign_cast` in `xvpe-collections-map`, reached through `xvpe-collections-persistent`; `D-016` records that the quarantine confines the dependency *edge* but not the toolchain floor that edge carries. Different crate, different axis, same shape, and both were found only by going and looking.

The abbreviated `rev` is not the defect and is not treated as one. `Cargo.lock` resolves it to `8ff98a8fd478750ca4f8a96ffd7174db902ffd0f`, so the abbreviation is latent rather than live, and rewriting it would churn the lock for no measured gain.
items.done_when:
`D-007` records the bump as the measurement the manifest says a pin exists to produce: which commit to which, that the four named crates were unchanged, that `xvpe-json-text` changed and how, and that the change was behaviourally inert -- measured rather than assumed, and dated.

It states the rule that measurement forces: the surface a rev bump must be measured against is the closure `Cargo.lock` resolves, not the crates the manifest names, and it names the five so that the next session does not have to re-derive them. It records this as the second instance of the shape `D-016` named once, since one instance was judged not to need a guard and two is a different question.

A contract guard holds the four `rev` values to a single commit, so a partial bump -- the shape a hand edit inside an item about something else produces -- fails instead of adopting two commits at once. Proven by mutating the real manifest rather than a reconstruction, with every assertion shown able to fail.

It does not change the pin, does not touch `Cargo.lock`, and does not bump anything. The item is the record and the guard.

items.title: The commit KWB-72 bumped to is the one that falsified D-004's coverage finding, and two records still describe the commit before it
items.why:
`KWB-96` established that no record in this repository mentions `8ff98a8fd`, the commit `kwb-platform-xvpe` has pinned since `KWB-72`. This is the consequence, and it is sharper than the general case.

Measured 2026-09-13:

`coverage_vocabulary.rs`, `journal_reader.rs` and `observed_coverage.rs` first appear in `xvpe-event-journal` **at `8ff98a8fd`**. At `a7eee3c6e` there is no `CoverageVocabulary`, `ObservedCoverage` or `JournalReader` anywhere in XVPE's tools or in that crate. At `8ff98a8fd` both mining products import them, both declare a `CLAIM_COVERAGE` vocabulary, and `xvpe-brainstorm-synthesizer` dispatches a `coverage` command over `JournalReader` and `ObservedCoverage`.

So `D-004` v2's coverage finding -- *both mining products write an append-only journal that nothing reads back; no `coverage`, `resume` or `redundant` symbol exists in either* -- was **true when it was written** against `a7eee3c6e`, and was made false by the very bump `KWB-72` performed. The pin moved onto the commit that answered the record, and nothing connected the two.

**`KWB-95`'s amendment is late by one commit, and that is mine to correct.** It unstranded the entry against `xvpe-corpus-ledger` at `7ec036c52`, which is correct and is a second instrument. It is not the first, and it is not the one this repository can reach: a reader of `D-004` v3 would conclude the evidence needs a bump to see, when the capability has been inside the adopted commit since `KWB-72`.

`D-014` carries the same staleness in the paragraph least able to afford it. Its *Measured at the pinned commit, after first measuring the wrong thing* passage says *re-taken from `a7eee3c6e`, which is what `kwb-platform-xvpe` pins*, and reports `journal_record.rs` and a reader beside it as **untracked** -- another session's in-flight work rather than the dependency. The pin is `8ff98a8fd`; `journal_record.rs` is tracked there and `JournalReader` is exported from the crate root. A paragraph written to warn against reading a sibling's working tree and calling it the dependency is now itself reporting the wrong commit, and it was `KWB-72` -- the item that wrote this record's own latest amendment -- that moved the pin out from under it.

**`D-014`'s refusal is not affected and this item does not touch it.** Measured at `a7eee3c6e`, `8ff98a8fd` and `7ec036c52`: `EventJournal::Write(&mut self, record: &JsonObjectWriter)` returns unit at all three. The failure contract that grounds the refusal is unchanged, and *Settled by: a fallible write in `xvpe-event-journal`* still states the condition correctly.
items.done_when:
`D-004` is at version 4. Its coverage entry names `8ff98a8fd` as where the capability arrived -- `xvpe-event-journal`'s `CoverageVocabulary`, `JournalReader` and `ObservedCoverage`, consumed by both mining products and dispatched as a `coverage` command -- and says plainly that this is the commit already pinned, so reaching it needs no bump. It says `xvpe-corpus-ledger` at `7ec036c52` is a second instrument and a later one, and it says that version 3 dated this wrongly and whose error that was.

`D-014` is at version 4. The *Measured at the pinned commit* paragraph is corrected where it is wrong -- the pin is `8ff98a8fd`, and `journal_record.rs` and the reader are tracked there -- without disturbing the refusal, which is re-measured at all three commits and restated as still correct. The correction is written as an amendment rather than an edit in place, because what the paragraph got right about method is worth keeping visible beside what the pin did to it.

Neither amendment moves a held subject, decides adoption, or changes the pin.

items.title: The one dependency edge that changes a default is the only one the manifest does not explain, and it is the only one no compile protects
items.why:
`kwb-platform-xvpe` is where `D-007`'s quarantine is implemented, and its manifest reasons out loud about everything except the one choice a reader would question.

Every dependency there carries a paragraph. `xvpe-clock`'s says the feature choice explicitly -- *`default-features` stays on, deliberately. `HostedWallClock` is behind `std`, and without it this crate would adopt a port with no implementation -- measured at this commit, proved by naming the types rather than by this manifest listing the crate.* `xvpe-collections-persistent` carries `default-features = false`, the only non-default feature setting in the file, and no comment at all.

Measured at `8ff98a8fd`, 2026-09-13:

**The setting is load-bearing, not decoration.** `xvpe-collections-persistent` and `xvpe-collections-map` both carry `#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]`, so the setting compiles them freestanding, and `xvpe-collections-map` gates `pub use standard_hash_map::StandardHashMap` behind `std`, so the setting also removes a type from the surface this workspace sees. `cargo tree -f "{p} [{f}]"` confirms the resolution: `xvpe-collections-persistent []`, `xvpe-collections-map []`, `xvpe-collections-sequence []`.

**The two settings are protected unequally, and neither fact is written down.** The clock's is guarded by construction: `pub use xvpe_clock::HostedWallClock as SystemClock` in `src/lib.rs` fails to compile the moment that crate's defaults go off, which is what the manifest means by *proved by naming the types*. The collections setting has no equivalent. Deleting `default-features = false` compiles cleanly, turns `std` on, and adds `StandardHashMap` to the surface -- and nothing fails, because nothing here names it. A future session removing that line to tidy the manifest gets no signal at all.

**The other two edges' feature state is inert, which is worth saying so nobody copies the clock's reasoning onto them.** `xvpe-corpus-text` and `xvpe-ai-inference` each declare `std = ["xvpe-primitives/std"]` and nothing else, and their own documentation says the crate needs nothing from std. `xvpe-primitives` resolves to `[std]` regardless, because those two and the clock all enable it and Cargo unifies features across the graph. So for those two, defaults on or off changes nothing about their own code.

This completes what `KWB-96` started rather than repeating it. That item established the closure is nine crates and not four; this establishes that the closure is a set of *features* as well as a set of crates, and that one feature choice in it is unexplained and unprotected.
items.done_when:
`crates/platform/kwb-platform-xvpe/Cargo.toml` explains the `default-features = false` on `xvpe-collections-persistent` in the register the rest of the file already uses: what the setting buys -- two crates compiled freestanding and `StandardHashMap` kept off the surface -- and that deleting it is silent, unlike the clock's setting, which a `pub use` fails on. Stating the absence of a guard is part of the remedy rather than an omission in it, on `KWB-94`'s reasoning: a test asserting the manifest contains a line it is the manifest's job to contain proves nothing a reader of the line does not already know.

`D-007` records the feature measurement beside the closure measurement it already carries, since which features resolve is part of what the pin adopts and the record now says the closure is the surface a bump must be measured against. It names the resolved feature sets, says the clock's choice is compile-protected and the collections choice is not, and says the other two edges are inert.

The pin does not move, `Cargo.lock` is not touched, and no feature setting changes -- the measurement says all four are currently right. This item makes them legible, not different.

items.title: The README's transcript had never been run, and the one block a reader compares against shows half the lines the binary prints
items.why:
`KWB-45` gave this repository a *Trying it* section and nothing has ever checked it against the binary. Run end to end for the first time, 2026-09-13, from a clean store with two files of my own text:

**Three of the four blocks match exactly.** The first `kwb admit` printed `source`, `coverage`, `concepts`, `claims`, `citations`, `refused`, `documents`, `knowledge` in that order, the field names and values the README shows. `kwb-mcp ./corpus neighbours entropy` printed `concept`, `claim` and two `cited` lines with the scope in brackets. `kwb history --store ./corpus --through 3` printed `through    3 of 6`, `concepts 1`, `claims 1`, `citations 1`, `held 1` -- **identical to the README, count for count**, which also means that block was produced from a real run rather than composed.

**The product does what the section claims.** Two different files, two different content addresses, one claim carrying two citations. That is `D-002`'s source exclusion working end to end through the CLI, and it had been asserted here and never demonstrated.

**The second `admit` block is wrong.** The README shows four lines -- `source`, `concepts`, `claims`, `citations` -- and the binary prints eight. `coverage`, `refused`, `documents` and `knowledge` are missing with no ellipsis or any other mark, so a reader who runs the command sees four lines the document does not account for and has no way to tell an abridgement from a change in behaviour. `crates/host/kwb-cli/src/main.rs` prints all eight unconditionally, one `println!` each, in a single run beginning at `source`.

This is the same family as `KWB-61` and `KWB-67` -- the README and the binary disagreeing about the binary's own surface -- and the same remedy applies. It differs in the direction of the drift: those were about which verbs exist, and this is about what one of them says.
items.done_when:
The second `admit` block in `README.md` shows what the binary prints: all eight fields, in the order they are printed. The transcript stays a transcript rather than becoming a summary.

A guard in `tests/contract` holds every `kwb admit` block in `README.md` to the label sequence `kwb-cli` actually prints, with the sequence **read from the source** rather than listed in the test, so the guard cannot drift from the binary the way the README did. It fails if the binary gains or loses a report field and the README does not follow, and it fails if a README block abridges one. Proven by mutating the real README and the real source, with every assertion shown able to fail, including the one that proves the guard read anything at all.

It does not guard the hashes. Those are content addresses of files the README does not ship, so a reader cannot reproduce them and the guard must not pretend otherwise -- that is a separate question about whether the transcript should be made reproducible, and it is not this item.

items.title: Nothing requires a record to name the commit this workspace actually adopts, so a rev bump can land with no record of what it changed
items.why:
`D-004` names this mechanism and deliberately does not build it: *A record that states the SHA it was measured against is making a claim that expires, and nothing here holds that claim against the pin* -- *named here and not built, because building it is its own item and this one is a re-sort.* This is that item.

The failure already happened and cost three corrections. `KWB-72` bumped `kwb-platform-xvpe` from `a7eee3c6e361371b269217201233a2e7d7e36122` to `8ff98a8fd` inside an item whose subject was `D-014`'s last deferral. No record named the new commit. `D-004` went on calling coverage-and-exhaustion **stranded** while the capability that unstranded it sat inside the adopted commit; `D-014`'s most careful paragraph went on naming `a7eee3c6e` as *what `kwb-platform-xvpe` pins*; and `KWB-96` found the manifest names four crates where the lock resolves nine. `KWB-95`, `KWB-96` and `KWB-97` cleaned that up by hand. Nothing stops it recurring on the next bump.

The manifest states the rule itself, beside the pin: *Bumping the `rev` is a decision, not maintenance. What changed between two commits of another repository is exactly what a pinned dependency exists to make visible.* It is stated and unenforced.

Measured 2026-09-13: `D-004`, `D-007` and `D-014` now name `8ff98a8fd`, so the guard specified below passes as the tree stands. Between `KWB-72` and `KWB-96` it would have failed, which is the window this exists to close.
items.done_when:
A guard in `tests/contract` asserts that **the rev `kwb-platform-xvpe` pins appears in at least one record under `docs/records/`**. The rev is read from the manifest, never written as a literal in the test, so the guard cannot drift from the pin the way the records did.

**What it must NOT assert, and this is the substance of the specification.** Not that every SHA cited in `docs/` equals the pin. A record reporting a measurement taken at an older commit is stating history and is correct to keep it -- `D-004` version 2 measured at `a7eee3c6e` and that sentence is still true. Demanding equality would force rewriting the record of what was measured when, which is the opposite of what this repository does with amendments. The floor is that the **current** pin is written down somewhere, because that is what was missing.

**A parser hazard to defeat rather than discover.** A scan keyed on "a hex-looking token" also matches the unix timestamps and GitHub run identifiers already present in `docs/` -- `1789254256` and `34766510019` both match `[0-9a-f]{9,}`. Key the search on the manifest's rev **value**, not on a shape.

Sanity assertions in the KWB-44 pattern, because a guard that reads nothing passes for the wrong reason: it fails if no rev was read from the manifest, and fails if fewer than ten records were read.

Proven by mutating the real files rather than a reconstruction, with every assertion shown able to fail: pointing the manifest at a rev no record names fails it, and each sanity assertion is fired in turn. Restore the manifest byte-identical afterwards and confirm with `git diff --stat`.

Out of scope, and deliberately: amending `D-004` to record that the mechanism it named is now built. That is a record change, which is the design half, and it follows the audit rather than riding along with the implementation.

items.title: The README's transcript prints content addresses of files it does not ship, and nothing tells a reader which lines they can reproduce
items.why:
`KWB-99` ran the *Trying it* section end to end for the first time and deferred this by name: *it does not guard the hashes -- those are content addresses of files the README does not ship, so a reader cannot reproduce them and the guard must not pretend otherwise -- that is a separate question about whether the transcript should be made reproducible, and it is not this item.* This is that question.

What `KWB-99` measured is what makes the gap precise. Three of the four blocks reproduce exactly: the field names and their order, and `kwb history --store ./corpus --through 3` printing `through    3 of 6` with the same four counts, **identical to the README count for count** from a corpus built out of two files of entirely different text. What does not reproduce is the `source` line of each `admit` block and the `cited` lines under `kwb-mcp`, because those are content addresses of `callen.txt` and `kittel.txt`, which are not in this repository.

So a reader who follows the section sees most of it match and two kinds of line differ, with nothing saying which outcome is expected. That is the same defect shape as the second `admit` block `KWB-99` corrected -- output a reader compares against that does not describe what they will see -- arriving through values rather than through fields.
items.done_when:
`README.md` says, adjacent to the transcript, which parts of it a reader reproduces and which depend on their own files: the field names, their order and the counts are reproducible; the `source` and `cited` values are content addresses of the reader's own bytes and will differ. Two sentences is the right size.

**The decision, which is made here rather than left to the implementation: do not ship fixture files, and do not change the digests shown.** Shipping a `callen.txt` and a `kittel.txt` would make the digests reproducible and it is the wrong trade. It buys a property no reader needs -- the section exists to demonstrate that two sources become one claim with two citations, and that is carried by the counts, which already reproduce -- and it costs a maintenance surface, because every digest in the README would then be a projection of two files through the normalizer, regenerated whenever normalization changes, with nothing holding it in step. The README already tells the reader the address depends on the file: *A different book, a different source address.* What is missing is saying the same thing about its own transcript.

`cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests` stays green, which means the `KWB-99` guard still passes: the eight report fields and their order are not to be disturbed by this edit.

No fixture files are added, no digest in the README changes, and nothing under `crates/` is touched.

items.title: The board carried no widened field, so every ledger verb refused it
items.why: OD-LEDGER-039 added LedgerItem::widened at schema 6 with no serde default, deliberately, so that a newer build meeting an older file is stopped per field rather than silently accepting a row missing it. Nomos migrated its own board in that commit and this one was not migrated, so every nomos build since 2026-09-14 refused this file outright and no work verb ran here. Nothing in this repository reported it: the only in-repo reader of the board reads it as text, so the gate stayed green on a file the tool that manages it would not parse. This item is written after the repair it records, which is the only order available, because no verb that could add an item could parse the board it would be added to.
items.done_when: Every item in work/ledger.json carries a widened field, nomos work validate exits 0 against it, and stripping that field back off reproduces the previous file byte-for-byte so that nothing else changed. schema_version is not hand-edited.

KWB-103 holds that failure. Re-claim and finish this once the gate is green; the work itself needs nothing further.

items.title: The gate's lint step has never executed, and the first time it ran it was red
items.why: OD-GATE-001 measured six workflow runs that completed in four or five seconds with empty steps arrays, on an account billing condition, so no gate step has ever executed against this repository. nomos work finish derives its lint step from gate.yml and runs it before any item predicate, which makes it the first enforcement that step has ever had here. It exited 101 at HEAD: kwb-source-guards trips three findings the workspace sets to warn at clippy pedantic and the gate raises to deny, on Crate_Sources and Mutating_Public_Methods in tests/guards/src/lib.rs. Until that is green no item can be finished through the ledger at all, because finish refuses before it reaches a predicate. KWB-102 is the first item to hit this and its repair is already committed at f557d15.
items.done_when: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings exits 0 over the workspace. The three findings are answered in the crate's own voice rather than silenced, and any suppression carries the justification this repository already requires of one. nomos work finish then reaches an item's predicate instead of refusing before it.

items.title: Domain vocabulary has one semantic authority, generalizing D-011 B7 from relation algebra
items.why: D-011 B7 decided that a relation's algebra belongs to its kind rather than to a registry consulted by convention, so a graph algorithm cannot receive a relation whose algebra it has not checked. That is one instance of a wider rule this repository has not stated. The prototype paid for its absence: YAML packs and hand-written IDomainModule classes each declared the same discipline, and a drift test was written to compensate for two descriptions of one thing. Deciding the rule before the first package exists costs a record; deciding it after costs a migration. D-011 Part C holds the pack format downstream, so this decides authority and names no carrier.
items.done_when: A new record generalizes D-011 B7 from relation algebra to domain vocabulary: one authoritative declaration owns entity kinds, relation kinds and the rest of the declarative vocabulary, and executable validators, inference providers, extractors, projections, generated code and documentation refer to it by stable identity rather than redeclaring what they consume. It states that the carrier, serialization, package shape and loading mechanism remain undecided, and says generalizes rather than amends, because D-011's decision is unchanged. D-011 gains the reciprocal relates-to relation and a Referenced By section, with no amendment section and no version bump, and the new record carries its own Referenced By. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: The shared source reader is non-recursive, and the two guards built on it assert an absence
items.why: kwb_source_guards::Crate_Sources reads manifest_directory/src with a single non-recursive read_dir, the same shape that blinded kwb-domain's liveness guard in KWB-108. Two guards are built on it: kwb-store's one-door test and kwb-retrieval's read-only test, both of which pair it with Mutating_Public_Methods to assert that no public method takes &mut self. Measured 2026-09-21, both crates' src directories are flat, so neither guard is blind today and this is a latent hazard rather than a live failure. It is the dangerous polarity of the same defect. The liveness guard requires a count of exactly one, so losing sight of the tree made it fail loudly; these require a count of zero, so losing sight of part of the tree makes them pass. The crate's own assert that sources is not empty catches total blindness and cannot catch partial blindness, which is the case a file split produces. kwb-domain, kwb-ingest, kwb-retrieval and the rest already hold subdirectories under src, so the arrangement this reader assumes is one the workspace has already stopped keeping.
items.done_when: Crate_Sources reads every .rs file under the crate's src at any depth, so that splitting a file into a subdirectory cannot narrow what a guard built on it sees. The behaviour is proved by a fixture tree carrying a source below the top level, which the reader must return and which a non-recursive read would miss, so the test fails if the recursion is removed. kwb-store's one-door test and kwb-retrieval's read-only test still pass and still fail when given a mutating method. This shares tests/guards/src/lib.rs with KWB-103, whose clippy findings sit on the very functions this changes, so one holder should take both in one pass and do this one first: the panics documentation KWB-103 owes Crate_Sources describes the surface this item rewrites. cargo test --workspace passes.

items.title: Normalize_Text deletes a line break standing alone between two words, so a reflowed line is an edit after all
items.why: Fold_Character asks is_control before is_whitespace. A line feed, a tab, a carriage return and U+0085 are both, so they are deleted rather than collapsed: measured 2026-09-24 by running kwb-model, Normalize_Text("a\nb\tc\r\nd") returns "abcd". That contradicts the function's own contract (a reflowed line, a changed line ending, or a model that indents differently is not an edit) and fuses two words into one token, so two readings of one sentence that differ only in where a line broke derive two claim identities. Test_Reflowed_Text_Should_Not_Change_Identity passes on the defect because its fixture's line break is followed by two spaces, which supply the run the deleted break should have. XVPE's xvpe-content-identity, generalized from this crate byte for byte on 2026-09-24, asks whitespace first; the seven identities it pins agree with this crate because none of their inputs holds control-class whitespace standing alone. No stored identity moves: every stored text is already a normalizer output, which holds no control character and no doubled space, and the corrected function returns such text unchanged, so every published log replays to the same addresses. What changes is only a future admission of raw text with a lone line break, which will now derive the identity its reflowed twin always had.
items.done_when: Fold_Character asks is_whitespace before is_control, so every Unicode White_Space character including U+0009-U+000D and U+0085 joins the pending run, and every other control character, the unit separator among them, is still removed. A test normalizes "a\nb", "a\tb", "a\r\nb" and "a\u{85}b" to "a b", and was shown to fail with the two checks put back in their present order. Test_Reflowed_Text_Should_Not_Change_Identity gains a case whose line break has no neighbouring space. A test asserts Normalize_Text is the identity function on its own output for every input the crate's tests use, which is the argument that no stored identity moves. Test_Normalize_Should_Strip_Control_Characters and the field-boundary forgery test pass unmodified. Forbidden: folding case; adding any normalization beyond the order of the two checks; rewriting, re-deriving or migrating any stored record; merging an identity derived before the fix with one derived after it, which would be a merge on a resemblance D17 says needs evidence. cargo test --workspace passes.

abandoned.reason:
Stopped rather than improvised: the specification is exact, and following it makes the item's own predicate red in a file the item does not reserve.

`Fold_Character` was put in the `done_when`'s order -- `is_whitespace` before `is_control` -- and `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` was run. Exactly one test fails, and it is not in this item's territory: `crates/retrieval/kwb-retrieval/tests/one_vocabulary.rs:179`, `Test_A_Control_Character_In_A_Query_Should_Be_Stripped_And_Not_Read_As_A_Space`, which asserts `Claims_Matching("isolated\tsystem").is_empty()` with the message "a tab was read as a space, so the search is splitting the query itself instead of normalizing it the way the claim's text was normalized".

The mechanism is direct, not incidental: `matching::Words_Of` is `Normalize_Text(query).split_whitespace()`, so a tab that joins the pending run makes that query the two words `isolated` and `system`, and they are both in the corpus claim's text.

That assertion is a deliberate claim about what a query *means*, argued in the test's own words as the surprising case and "asserted rather than excused". Reversing it is a semantic ruling rather than a maintenance edit: after the fix, a caller who searches with a tab between two words gets the claim, where the guard says no claim's identity was ever derived from text that would match. The item's `why` and `done_when` argue only about identity derivation and never mention the query surface, retrieval, or a search, so its closing clause -- "cargo test --workspace passes" -- is false as written, and the premise behind it, that this change is workspace-neutral, does not hold.

Measured rather than supposed, and nothing was left in the tree. `derivation.rs` is restored byte-identically: sha256 aca323860bd0dd6539d72c45b1769fd31f0269b4c2dd5bb63a0b72bf97e10d80 both before and after. With the fix applied, 87 of the 88 workspace suites pass and the only failing assertion anywhere is the one above -- which independently corroborates the item's "no stored identity moves", including every identity the domain, ingest, store, retrieval, CLI and MCP suites pin.

Wanted from the design phase, and not this session's to decide: either the territory widened to that file together with a ruling on what the search should now answer for a tab, or a decision that a tab stays a control character and this item is declined.

items.title: kwb-mcp names five tools and speaks no protocol, while the adopted XVPE revision already ships the MCP handshake
items.why: kwb-mcp is an MCP host that prints 'No transport is wired': its tools are reachable only as command-line arguments, so no agent can call them, which is the only reason an MCP host exists. At the revision kwb-platform-xvpe already pins (8ff98a8fd), and unchanged since, XVPE ships xvpe-remote-call (ToolCatalogStrategy, ToolDescriptor, ToolAnswer) and xvpe-remote-call-backend-json (Serve_Tools: line-framed JSON-RPC 2.0 with initialize, tools/list, tools/call and ping, protocol version 2024-11-05). Nomos's nomos-mcp serves its own catalogue exactly this way, ported down on 2026-09-10 so that no product writes the handshake twice. Under D-135 protocol code with no knowledge semantics is XVPE's, and under the ecosystem-substrate placement rule (f:/repos/xvpe/docs/plans/programs/ecosystem-substrate) a product keeps its catalogue and adopts the wire. The cost is measurable and is not zero: the JSON backend depends on serde and serde_json, so the Cargo.lock closure grows, and D-007's amendment says the closure is what an adoption is measured against.
items.done_when: kwb-platform-xvpe adopts xvpe-remote-call and xvpe-remote-call-backend-json at the same rev as its other four crates, so the single-rev guard in tests/contract holds, and re-exports only what kwb-mcp uses. kwb-mcp implements ToolCatalogStrategy over the existing TOOLS registry: every descriptor's name and sentence is projected from TOOLS rather than restated, and every call is answered by the same Answer_Tool_Call the command-line path uses, so the two surfaces cannot disagree about what a tool says. kwb-mcp serves over stdio through Serve_Tools when asked to, and its existing command-line form keeps working. A test drives initialize, tools/list and tools/call over in-memory lines and asserts tools/list names exactly the tools in TOOLS and a call's text equals what the command line prints for the same tool and store. kwb-retrieval's read-only test passes unmodified. The packages the closure gained are listed in a D-007 amendment. Forbidden: a second tool registry beside TOOLS; any tool with a write path; naming an XVPE crate anywhere but kwb-platform-xvpe; a path dependency on XVPE; moving the rev. cargo test --workspace passes.

items.title: kwb-model derives through XVPE's content identity, so one derivation and one normalizer serve both products, and the refusal SHA-256 owes is surfaced rather than wrapped
items.why: D-018 decides this item and holds what was measured. kwb-model's Derivation, ContentIdentity, Exclusion, Sealed, IdentityError and Normalize_Text were generalized into XVPE's xvpe-content-identity on 2026-09-24, which reproduces seven identities this repository published through two independent SHA-256 implementations. Two copies of one derivation drift, and KWB-111 is that drift already measured: the normalizer here deletes a lone line break XVPE's collapses. Under D-135 an identity scheme carries no knowledge semantics -- its definition never mentions a claim, a concept or a source -- so the scheme is XVPE's, and the kinds and fields this repository derives under it stay here. Measured 2026-09-24 against XVPE c700bcf83: the public surfaces match name for name -- the same items, the same methods, IdentityError with the same two variants, the same 64-character lowercase rendering, so a KnowledgeReferenceId (Nomos D-137) keeps its value and its shape; no crate here names Derivation as a type. One difference decides this item's size. XVPE's Seal returns Result<Sealed, InputTooLong>, because SHA-256 is defined only for messages under 2^64 bits and a streaming derivation can be fed past that; kwb-model's Seal returns Sealed, and past that bound sha2 wraps the length, which would give two different inputs one identity. This repository denies panic paths, so the refusal can only be propagated: Claim::About, Concept::Named, Assertion::By and kwb-store's Document::Of seal, and 51 files across eight crates call them or Seal (23 production call sites of the four constructors, about 209 in tests). Adopting xvpe-content-identity into kwb-platform-xvpe adds exactly two packages to Cargo.lock at c700bcf83 -- xvpe-content-identity and xvpe-algorithms-hashing; everything beneath them already arrives through xvpe-collections-persistent -- and sha2, which only kwb-model uses, leaves.
items.done_when: kwb-platform-xvpe adopts xvpe-content-identity at the rev its other XVPE crates pin, behind a cargo feature that enables that crate and nothing else, while every XVPE crate it already adopts moves behind its default features so each existing consumer keeps what it has. kwb-model depends on kwb-platform-xvpe with default features off and that one feature on, so its own closure gains no clock, inference, chunker or persistent map, and it keeps every public name it has -- Derivation, ContentIdentity, Exclusion, Sealed, IdentityError, Normalize_Text, IDENTITY_BYTES, IDENTITY_CHARACTERS -- as re-exports of XVPE's, plus InputTooLong; it holds no SHA-256, normalizer or derivation of its own, and sha2 leaves both its manifest and the workspace's. InputTooLong is propagated: Claim::About, Concept::Named, Assertion::By and Document::Of return Result, and each production caller passes it with ? to the nearest function that already returns a Result, giving any function between them a Result where it has none; a test builds its fixtures through a helper that expects with a named message. No pinned identity changes: no hex string, fixture log or golden file is edited, and Test_Replay_Records_Should_Hold_What_The_Original_Held and KWB-111's tests pass unmodified. Cargo.lock gains exactly the two packages D-018 measured and loses sha2 with whatever only sha2 brought; a different delta is a stop, reported with the packages, because it means D-018 is wrong. cargo test --workspace passes. Forbidden: unwrap, expect or panic outside tests to discharge InputTooLong; a sentinel, zero or wrapped identity for an over-long input; any change to what an identity renders as; a second derivation or normalizer left beside XVPE's; naming an XVPE crate anywhere but kwb-platform-xvpe; a path dependency; moving the rev.

items.title: A visitor to the GitHub repository cannot tell what KWB is for, because the page GitHub shows is the workspace authority written for agents
items.why: The owner asked for the repository to be presentable to recruiters and other visitors, who should come away knowing the goals of the project. The root README.md is the authority AGENTS.md routes to for what exists, its tables are generated and checked by tests/contract, and it opens with record identifiers a visitor cannot use; rewriting it for visitors would weaken that authority or copy it. GitHub shows .github/README.md in preference to the root README.md, so a visitor page can live there and leave README.md exactly as it is. The page is prose about what KWB means and is for, which is the design phase: it was authored at docs/github-landing-page.md in the commit that added this item. Placing it at .github/README.md is outside the design phase write territory, and that placement is all this item is.
items.done_when: The file .github/README.md exists and is byte-identical to docs/github-landing-page.md as committed alongside this item, renamed there through git so the draft no longer exists and its history follows it. No other file changes: README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/records and every crate are untouched. The predicate resolves every relative link and repository path the page cites from its new location. Forbidden: rewording, re-wrapping or reformatting any line of the page (a content change is a design question and goes back to the design phase as a new item); editing README.md; adding a route to the page in AGENTS.md; creating a directory under docs. The predicate deliberately reaches nothing in tests/contract, because no test reads .github/README.md; the loose file under docs is not a directory, so the docs-directory routing guard never saw it and does not see its removal.

Declined.reason: Declined by KWB-122 as false, not as inconvenient. Its done_when places docs/github-landing-page.md byte-identical to the draft committed alongside it at c2d8c24, and that draft stated five things false at 00dd02d: 18 decision records, where docs/records holds 22; following a citation returns the exact bytes, where nothing follows a citation; MCP serving as the next item on the board, where it is one ready item among several; kwb-extract listed under What works today, where no binary composes it; and five recorded data-loss incidents, where docs/corpus/prototype-incidents.md counts six. The draft is design-phase prose under docs/ and is corrected in the commit that declines this item; KWB-137 re-authors the placement against the corrected draft with the same terms and the same predicate.

items.title: The publication log keeps its lines through XVPE's record log, and a torn last line is refused instead of replayed as a publication nobody made
items.why: D-019 decides this and holds the clause-by-clause measurement. kwb-platform-std's FileRecordLog is the donor of xvpe-record-log and still keeps its own std::fs copy, so the two drift: at c700bcf83 XVPE's log refuses an empty record and a line break where this one trusts the domain, and reports a last line with no terminator as a torn tail where this one returns it as a record. That last difference is a defect here, not a style: Records() hands the fragment to Replay_Records, and a line cut inside its trailing field still parses -- as a different time, or at the untimed arity with a shortened last field (record_time.rs Timestamped_Fields) -- so a crash mid-append publishes something nobody published. Bytes already on disk are compatible: both sides write record plus LF, skip a blank line and drop a CR before the terminator. Measured 2026-09-25 at c700bcf83: adopting the log adds exactly xvpe-record-log, xvpe-file-system and xvpe-file-system-backend-system, none third-party, all at the rev kwb-platform-xvpe already pins. The store half is not this item: XVPE's store counted a directory as held until a fix XVPE made the same day, and it needs its own pin move once that fix is published (D-019).
items.done_when: kwb-platform-xvpe adopts xvpe-record-log, xvpe-file-system and xvpe-file-system-backend-system at the rev its other XVPE crates pin, behind one cargo feature that enables those three and nothing else, not among its defaults; kwb-platform-std depends on kwb-platform-xvpe with default features off and that feature on, so its closure gains no clock, inference, chunker or persistent map. kwb-platform-std's FileRecordLog keeps its name, At(path) -> Result<Self, StorageError> and its RecordLogStrategy impl, and keeps its lines through xvpe-record-log's FileRecordLog over the system file system; no std::fs, OpenOptions, BufReader or writeln! remains in file_record_log.rs. At still creates the log's directory and an empty file, through the injected file system rather than std::fs, so a store root holds publications.log after At exactly as it does today. Every XVPE refusal maps to StorageError::Refused with a doing that names the operation; a refusal kind XVPE adds later maps to Refused too, never a panic. The five tests in kwb-platform-std/tests/file_record_log.rs pass unmodified. New tests there, each written to fail first against the std::fs implementation where it can: a log whose last line lacks its terminator makes Records() Refused, and the refusal's text names how many complete records precede the fragment; Append of a record holding a line feed or a carriage return is Refused and leaves the file's bytes unchanged; a log file written byte for byte as today's implementation writes it, plus a CRLF-terminated line and a blank line, reads back the records today's implementation reads. Cargo.lock gains exactly those three packages and nothing else; a different delta is a stop, reported with the packages, because it means D-019's measurement is wrong. README.md's band and dependency statements match the new same-band edge. cargo test --workspace passes. Forbidden: XVPE's Close_Torn_Tail, or any other way of terminating, keeping or dropping a torn tail, since D-019 leaves repair undecided; mapping a torn tail to Ok; naming an xvpe_ crate anywhere but kwb-platform-xvpe; behaviour in kwb-platform-xvpe beyond re-exports; changing kwb-platform's RecordLogStrategy or StorageError; moving the log's path or file name; editing a test outside kwb-platform-std/tests/file_record_log.rs; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests; a path dependency; moving the rev; adopting xvpe-content-store, which is the store half's own item.

items.title: kwb-platform-std's DirectoryContentStore keeps its documents through XVPE's content store over the injected file system, and refuses an address that is not a content identity instead of calling it absent
items.why: D-019 decides it, and its 2026-09-27 amendment measured the revision. At f45a7b085 xvpe-content-store's DirectoryContentStore counts only a regular file as held, refuses a put onto a directory before writing anything, puts through a unique exclusive temporary synchronized before the rename, and removes a failed put's temporary; XVPE's file-system port can create a directory, so Under keeps its promise without a second route to the disk; and adopting the store adds exactly xvpe-content-store. Bytes already on disk are compatible: a document is <root>/<64 lowercase hex> holding the raw bytes on both sides, and XVPE pins that layout with a test of its own. Today's adapter keeps its documents through std::fs beside the port the publication log goes through after KWB-116, keeps a failed put's <address>.staged file, which D-019 retired as evidence nothing ever read and the race XVPE's unique temporaries remove, and accepts any string as an address, so a caller's malformed address reads as a true-sounding 'not held'.
items.done_when: kwb-platform-xvpe adopts xvpe-content-store at the rev its other XVPE crates pin, behind the cargo feature KWB-116 added for the log -- which then enables xvpe-content-store beside xvpe-record-log, xvpe-file-system and xvpe-file-system-backend-system, and nothing else -- and re-exports ContentStoreStrategy, ContentStoreError and DirectoryContentStore beside the log's re-exports, adding no behaviour. kwb-platform-std's DirectoryContentStore keeps its name, Under(root) -> Result<Self, StorageError> and its ContentStoreStrategy impl, and keeps its documents through xvpe-content-store's DirectoryContentStore over the system file system; no std::fs, OpenOptions or other route to the disk remains in directory_content_store.rs. Under creates the root through the port's Create_Directory, so the directory exists when Under returns, as it does today. Every address is parsed as a rendered content identity before the store is asked anything: an address that does not parse makes Holds, Put and Get each return StorageError::Refused with a cause naming the address -- never Absent, and never false. XVPE's Absent maps to StorageError::Absent carrying the address as the caller gave it; every other ContentStoreError, including a variant XVPE adds later (the enum is non_exhaustive), maps to StorageError::Refused with a doing that names the operation, never a panic. kwb-platform-std/tests/directory_content_store.rs addresses the store with rendered content identities instead of short strings and otherwise keeps every test's assertion: Under creates its directory; bytes read back unchanged; an absent address is refused as Absent; a repeat put is idempotent and leaves one file; a completed put leaves exactly the document's file. Test_A_Write_Should_Be_Staged_And_Renamed_Rather_Than_Written_In_Place, which asserts the kept .staged file D-019 retired, becomes a test that a put onto an address where a directory stands is Refused and leaves that directory in place with nothing else written beside it. New tests there, each written to fail first against today's implementation where it can: an address that is not a content identity is Refused by each of Holds, Put and Get; a directory holding documents written byte for byte as today's implementation writes them reads back the same bytes. The kwb-store suites that open a DirectoryContentStore (tests/document_store.rs, tests/one_door.rs) pass unmodified. Cargo.lock gains exactly xvpe-content-store and nothing else; a different delta is a stop, reported with the packages, because it means D-019's measurement is wrong. README.md's kwb-platform-xvpe row names the store beside what the crate already adopts. cargo test --workspace passes. For every verdict of met or diverges it authors implementation items with territory, a done_when naming what is forbidden, and a predicate selecting every crate it changes, and it specifies any XVPE step it needs in kwb-parity.md, X9 included. items.title: The epistemic layer the prototype measured on real books -- adjudication, grounding, corroboration with trust, the relation kernel -- has no verdict here, and D-004 holds half of it
items.why: Goal G5 of D-021, rows C-15 to C-22 and C-47 to C-54 of docs/corpus/prototype-capabilities.md. The prototype adjudicated each proposed claim against its concept's neighbourhood into four verdicts on a closed candidate list; gated on a found quote; counted support over distinct sources and never showed it without a trust grade (certified, candidate, suspect); calibrated its adjudicator with reference verdicts that name their labeler; measured a local model folding about 41 percent wrong, in one direction; and carried a 21-kind relation vocabulary with an executable constraint table, negative assertions that require a falsifier, and hypotheses that inference writes instead of edges. D-004 holds admission, the confidence model, promotion, corroboration and coverage exhaustion pending the reference miner's measurements, and holds the relation kernel where evidence is weak; D-011 states the kernel's requirements. XVPE publishes ClaimGrounding, QuoteVerification and ClaimLedger::Corroborated. KWB-105, the guard on vocabulary authority, belongs to this goal.

A row D-004 holds is verdicted deferred, naming the measurement it waits on and whether a copy in a scratch directory can supply it -- which the owner's words of 2026-09-24 allow -- or only a run the owner must release; it is not decided in order to close the goal. items.title: Thirteen of the prototype's fourteen enrichment stages have no verdict here, and the one this repository has runs inside admission
items.why: Goal G6 of D-021, rows C-23 and C-36 to C-45 of docs/corpus/prototype-capabilities.md. The prototype's enrichment chain ran fourteen stages -- embed, annotate, summarize, link concepts, harvest aliases, normalize, typed concept edges, identity judging, concept kind, subject taxonomy, proofs, the proof graph, exercises and concept synthesis -- incrementally, each committing alone and resuming from a coverage ledger, plus evidence weighting and evidence packs. The measured fact worth carrying is that fourteen null objects let every stage run with no model at all: remove the model and the feature still makes sense, or it is not a KWB feature. This repository links a claim to the concept its own reading named, inside one admission, and has none of the other stages.
items.done_when: A record verdicts C-23 and C-36 to C-45 by name. It decides which stages this repository has, the order they run in, and what each consumes and produces; how a stage resumes and what its coverage records; what each stage does with no model, stated per stage; and, for typed concept edges, which relation kinds it may emit while D-011 holds the kernel's closed vocabulary. For every verdict of met or diverges it authors implementation items with territory, a done_when naming what is forbidden, and a predicate selecting every crate it changes, and it specifies any XVPE step it needs in kwb-parity.md. Forbidden: a stage whose output a person could not produce in the model's place; a stage that commits another stage's work; merging concepts on a model's judgement of identity, which the prototype refused by writing SameConceptAs edges instead; a closed vocabulary D-011 holds. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: README.md says KWB means to link knowledge to the code that realises it, and no record decides whether KWB owns a code entity
items.why: Goal G6 of D-021, rows C-68 to C-72 of docs/corpus/prototype-capabilities.md. The prototype extracted code entities from two books behind a verbatim guard -- 798 entities and 22,316 links -- linked them to concepts by name, reported what a book explains and never implements and prints and never explains, and kept project spaces, decision notes, linked repositories and a drift check. README.md records the intent and says no record has decided what a code entity would be or whether KWB owns one. Nomos's ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 decides ownership between the four products by semantics and gives software engineering to Nomos; KWB owns rationale and decision context.
items.done_when: A record here decides, against ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 and D-135 as they read at a named Nomos revision, whether KWB owns a code entity, and if not, which product does and what KWB holds instead -- for example a reference by opaque identity, which D-137 in Nomos admits in the other direction. It verdicts C-68 to C-72 by name accordingly, project spaces and decision notes included, since they sit closer to KWB's decision context than to code. It authors implementation items for every verdict of met or diverges, with territory, a done_when naming what is forbidden, and a predicate selecting every crate it changes, and one Correction item that brings README.md's intended-and-not-built paragraph into line with the decision. Forbidden: a KWB crate that analyses source code, where the decision gives that to Nomos; editing Nomos's records; a code entity whose identity is a path, which the prototype used and which breaks a citation the moment a file moves. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Revision -- a derived thing going stale when what it came from changes -- is the product loop's steps 7 and 8, and D-006 states it with nothing computing it
items.why: Goal G7 of D-021, rows C-74 and C-75 of docs/corpus/prototype-capabilities.md. The corpus's product loop ends by recomputing derived connections and invalidating stale syntheses, and the prototype's own roadmap named derivation-dependency staleness, graph snapshots and merge preview as verified absent. D-006, from KWB-14, decides that a derivation declares what it was derived from and that staleness is computed, not stored; nothing here computes it. Publications already replay to any prefix, which is half of a snapshot.
items.done_when: A record decides what carries a derivation declaration in this repository; how staleness is computed for a changed input and for a retracted one; how a consumer learns of it without having to ask; what a snapshot is beyond a publication prefix; and what a merge preview shows before a merge is applied. It verdicts C-74 and C-75 by name, and authors implementation items with territory, a done_when naming what is forbidden, and a predicate selecting every crate it changes. Forbidden: storing a staleness flag, which D-006 refuses; deleting a derived artifact because an input changed (D17); applying a merge whose preview cannot be produced. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Comparing two bodies of knowledge and reconstructing a source from the graph are two of the nine operations, and neither the prototype nor this repository has either
items.why: Goal G7 of D-021, rows C-46, C-76 and C-77 of docs/corpus/prototype-capabilities.md. what-kwb-is-for.md names compare and reconstruct among the operations the prototype left essentially unbuilt: it compared two concepts and measured pairwise source overlap, and had no semantic diff and no reconstruction. The design corpus defines both (topic 415), and the prototype's roadmap lists semantic source diff and reconstruction as verified absent.
items.done_when: A record decides what compare takes and returns -- two concepts, two sources, two bodies of knowledge -- and what a semantic diff reports that a text diff cannot; and what reconstruct produces from the graph, and how its output is checked against the source it claims to reconstruct. It verdicts C-46, C-76 and C-77 by name, and authors implementation items with territory, a done_when naming what is forbidden, and a predicate selecting every crate it changes. Forbidden: a comparison that flattens a disagreement into one answer, which the corpus names among the product's exclusions; a reconstruction presented as the source rather than as the model's account of it. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Assessment -- what a person or an agent understands -- is one of the nine operations, and the prototype built learning paths by improvising and never verified an exercise
items.why: Goal G7 of D-021, rows C-73 and C-78 of docs/corpus/prototype-capabilities.md. The prototype built learning paths by improvising over seed concepts rather than traversing a prerequisite graph, extracted exercises, and left generated exercises and verified solutions unticked in every evidence column. The corpus defines assess as one of the workbench's nine operations.
items.done_when: A record decides what an assessment assesses, what counts as evidence of understanding, how a generated exercise is verified before it is shown, and whether a learning path is a traversal of the prerequisite edges G6 produces or something else. It verdicts C-73 and C-78 by name, and authors implementation items with territory, a done_when naming what is forbidden, and a predicate selecting every crate it changes. Forbidden: an exercise or solution shown unverified; a learning path presented as a traversal when it is a model's improvisation. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Nothing here composes an artifact from knowledge, and the essay that named the missing half says the core must know knowledge and evidence, not essays
items.why: Goal G7 of D-021, rows C-79 and C-80 of docs/corpus/prototype-capabilities.md. what-kwb-is-for.md records the essay's finding: the prototype synthesizes about one concept and composes nothing. KWB is two halves, knowledge compilation and artifact engineering -- intent, architecture, composition plan, evidence assignment, draft, evaluation findings, revision plan, candidate revision, validation, human decision, artifact version -- and an essay is one profile over general mechanisms, never a type in the core. The essay proposes crates for composition, evaluation and revision; the bands table has none, and README.md is the authority for bands.
items.done_when: A record decides the artifact-engineering half's shape: what an artifact intent, a composition plan and an evaluation finding are; how a revision is proposed, validated and decided by a person; how an artifact version carries its provenance back to the claims it used; and how a profile such as an essay configures the mechanisms without adding a type to the core. It decides whether new crates and bands are needed, and if so authors the item that adds them with README.md's bands table in its territory. It verdicts C-79 and C-80 by name, and authors implementation items with territory, a done_when naming what is forbidden, and a predicate selecting every crate it changes. Forbidden: a type named for one artifact kind, such as a thesis paragraph, in the core model; a revision applied without a recorded human decision; a composed artifact whose claims cannot be followed back to their citations. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: D21 has had no owner since this workspace grew a second crate, and two library crates have no production consumer, declared nowhere a check reads
items.why: Goal G0 of D-021, routed by KWB-122 from the D21 section of docs/corpus/prototype-incidents.md. D21 is the prototype's incident of a test that constrained a copy of a stage rather than the stage. Its section found the same failure one turn further out: a superseded stage, Enrichment/Discovery, kept alive by its own tests with no production consumer. It left D21 unowned until this repository had a second crate, and it now has fourteen members. Measured 2026-09-27 at 00dd02d from cargo metadata: every member with a library target is a normal dependency of another member that Workspace_Members admits, except two. kwb-contracts has no consumer by design; its crate documentation says it stays empty until the shape of a KWB-minted identifier is a decision. kwb-extract has no consumer; its crate documentation says the workspace deliberately does not depend on it and a composition root decides, and no composition root does, so its tests are green for a reader that nothing runs. Both are defensible. Neither is declared anywhere a check reads, so a third would join silently, which is the shape D21 names.
items.done_when: A test in tests/contract asserts that every member Workspace_Members admits that has a library target and no binary target is a normal dependency -- not a dev- or build-dependency -- of at least one other admitted member, or else declares unconsumed, with a reason, in its manifest's [package.metadata.kwb] table, the table band already lives in, read by the reader that already reads band. It fails in both directions: a crate with no consumer and no declaration fails naming the crate, and a crate that declares unconsumed while an admitted member depends on it fails naming the crate as a stale declaration. Dependencies are read from the members' own manifests, never from crate names written in the test. kwb-contracts declares, verbatim, unconsumed = "Band 0 admits nothing yet: its crate documentation says it stays empty until the shape of a KWB-minted identifier is a decision." and kwb-extract declares, verbatim, unconsumed = "No composition root uses the model reader yet: KWB-125 decides whether a model provider enters this workspace, and with it whether a root composes this crate." -- each under a comment in the style of the band comment above it. Proven by mutating the real files, with every assertion shown able to fail: deleting kwb-extract's declaration fails the test naming kwb-extract; adding a declaration to kwb-model, which five members depend on, fails it naming kwb-model; and a sanity assertion fails when fewer than ten admitted members with a library target were read, so a reader that found nothing cannot pass. Each mutated file is restored byte-identically, and git diff --stat afterwards shows only the intended change. Forbidden: adding a dependency to give a crate a consumer, since whether a root composes kwb-extract is KWB-125's decision; declaring unconsumed on any crate but these two; exempting a crate by its name or its band rather than by its targets; counting a crate under tests/ as a consumer. The predicate passes.

items.title: README.md says following a citation returns the document's exact bytes, and nothing follows a citation
items.why: Goal G0 of D-021, routed by KWB-122 from its item (5). Under the kwb-mcp neighbours transcript, README.md says each citation is the content address of the document the claim was read out of, so following one returns those exact bytes or fails loudly because they are gone. Measured 2026-09-27 at 00dd02d: no host calls DocumentStore::Read, so no command follows a citation; and Read consults the in-memory map only, so a store opened by a later process would answer NoSuchDocument for a document its durable medium holds -- failing loudly, for the wrong reason. KWB-123 decides whether a verb will follow a citation and whether Read consults the medium (C-65), and it waits on KWB-120. Until then README.md states as present a capability that does not exist. The first clause, that a citation is a content address, is true and stays.
items.done_when: In README.md, the two-sentence paragraph that begins Each citation is the and ends because they are gone. is replaced by exactly the following two sentences, wrapped at the file's line width like the paragraphs around it: Each citation is the **content address of the document the claim was read out of**, derived from that document's content rather than assigned. No command follows a citation back to the document yet; `D-021` routes that to goal G1. Nothing else in README.md changes: not the transcript, not its digests, not the paragraphs before or after it. Forbidden: rewording the replacement, which is a design question and goes back as a new item; editing any other file; adding a verb or touching crates/, which is KWB-123's decision. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: A visitor to the GitHub repository cannot tell what KWB is for, and the page drafted to tell them stated five things that were false
items.why: Goal G0 of D-021. Successor to KWB-115, which KWB-122 declined on 2026-09-27 because the draft it would have placed stated five things false at 00dd02d: 18 decision records, where docs/records holds 22; following a citation returns the exact bytes, where nothing follows a citation; MCP serving as the next item on the board, where it is one ready item among several; kwb-extract listed under What works today, where no binary composes it; and five recorded data-loss incidents, where docs/corpus/prototype-incidents.md counts six. The draft is corrected in the commit that added this item, and this item places that version. The owner asked for the repository to be presentable to recruiters and other visitors, who should come away knowing the goals of the project. The root README.md is the authority AGENTS.md routes to for what exists, its tables are generated and checked by tests/contract, and it opens with record identifiers a visitor cannot use; rewriting it for visitors would weaken that authority or copy it. GitHub shows .github/README.md in preference to the root README.md, so a visitor page can live there and leave README.md exactly as it is. The page is prose about what KWB means and is for, which is the design phase: it was authored at docs/github-landing-page.md in the commit that added KWB-115 and corrected in the commit that added this item. Placing it at .github/README.md is outside the design phase write territory, and that placement is all this item is.
items.done_when: The file .github/README.md exists and is byte-identical to docs/github-landing-page.md as committed alongside this item, renamed there through git so the draft no longer exists and its history follows it. No other file changes: README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/records and every crate are untouched. The predicate resolves every relative link and repository path the page cites from its new location. Forbidden: rewording, re-wrapping or reformatting any line of the page (a content change is a design question and goes back to the design phase as a new item); editing README.md; adding a route to the page in AGENTS.md; creating a directory under docs. The predicate deliberately reaches nothing in tests/contract, because no test reads .github/README.md; the loose file under docs is not a directory, so the docs-directory routing guard never saw it and does not see its removal.

Declined.reason: Declined by the 2026-10-03 audit as false, not as inconvenient. Its done_when places the visitor page byte-identical to the draft committed alongside it, and that draft has gone false since: KWB-112 made kwb-mcp serve its five tools over MCP, so the page's line that serving them is specified work on the board is wrong, and its figures were September's. KWB-176 corrects the draft. KWB-178 re-authors the placement to place the draft as it stands when claimed, so a later correction no longer needs a decline.

items.title: The liveness guard carries its own copy of the source reader the guards crate exists to hold once, and that reader's depth test cannot see its top level
items.why: Goal G0 of D-021, from the audit of KWB-108 and KWB-110 on 2026-09-28. tests/guards/src/lib.rs says the reading lives there once because, written twice, it was two copies a fix had to reach. crates/domain/kwb-domain/tests/one_liveness.rs carries a second copy, and it was exactly that: KWB-108 and KWB-110 each repaired the same one-level read_dir, as two items, in two commits. The two walks now differ only in that the liveness guard's returns each file's path relative to src. KWB-108 reserved only the test file, so it could not remove the copy, and met its done_when. Separately, KWB-110's Test_The_Source_Reader_Should_Read_Below_The_Top_Level has a second assertion looking for a source that contains Top_Level, and the nested fixture's Below_The_Top_Level contains it, so that assertion holds whenever the first does. Its documentation says it proves the top-level file arrives too, and nothing does: a reader that descended but skipped the top level would pass.
items.done_when: kwb-source-guards offers one reader that returns every .rs file under a crate's src at any depth together with its path relative to src, separators written as /, and Crate_Sources is expressed through that reader rather than beside it, so the directory walk exists once in the workspace. The crate documentation's account of who uses it names every crate that does. kwb-domain reaches it as a dev-dependency declared the way kwb-store declares it, under a comment saying why, and one_liveness.rs's Crate_Sources and Collect_Sources are deleted in its favour; Test_The_Crate_Should_Define_Liveness_Exactly_Once asserts what it asserts today and passes. The depth test's second assertion is keyed on something only the top-level fixture carries, such as the whole text of that file or the path the reader returns for it, and the documentation above both assertions says truthfully what each rules out. Proven by mutation, each mutated file restored byte-identically: making the walk skip files at the top level fails the depth test's second assertion; deleting the recursion fails its first; and deleting the recursion also fails the liveness guard, which now reads through the shared reader. Forbidden: a third copy of the walk anywhere; changing what any guard built on the reader asserts; moving the reader into a production crate; adding a normal dependency to kwb-domain. cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast passes.

items.why: Goal G1 of D-021, from the audit of KWB-100 on 2026-09-28. The failure message of Test_The_Adopted_Revision_Should_Be_Named_By_A_Record says D-005's precedent is the record for the decision that moved it. D-005 adopts the Nomos ledger schema and never mentions a revision. That message is the only thing a session sees when the pin moves without a record, so it sends the session to the wrong authority at exactly the moment it needs the right one. D-007 is the decision that the pin is a revision and a bump is a decision; D-018 is a record that writes a move down, 8ff98a8fd to c700bcf83, in the record of the decision that needs it.
items.done_when: The failure message names D-007 as the record that makes a bump a decision and D-018 as the precedent for writing a moved revision into the record of the decision that moves it, and no longer names D-005. Nothing else in the guard changes: what it reads, what it asserts, its floor, and its other messages. Forbidden: naming any record the message does not route to correctly; writing a revision into the test as a literal. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.
