items.title: Move the XVPE pin from c700bcf83 to 726aa3fee, because every earlier XVPE commit left GitHub and a fresh clone of this repository cannot build
items.why: Amended 2026-10-01 by D-007's 2026-10-01 amendment: 7471a1c9d itself left GitHub when XVPE's history was folded into one commit, so the target is 726aa3fee. Every XVPE crate this closure adopts, and the three the move adds, is byte-identical at the two commits, and xvpe-clock differs only in documentation, so the measurement below, taken at 7471a1c9d, holds at 726aa3fee. D-007's 2026-09-30 amendment decides this and holds the measurement. XVPE's history was restarted on 2026-09-30 and every commit this repository has pinned left GitHub with the old one, c700bcf83 included, so this workspace resolves XVPE only from a warm cargo git cache and a fresh clone cannot build. KWB-117 and KWB-119 planned two moves, to d6f075c14 and then f45a7b085; both targets are gone, and this one move to 7471a1c9d replaces them. Measured 2026-09-30 on a scratch clone of a3725be, toolchain 1.87.0. The source changes the move needs are the four KWB-117 and KWB-119 already measured -- the replay fixture expects RequestFingerprint::Of_Request's Result; ReplayInference and ReplayRecording are re-exported at xvpe_ai_inference's crate root because its strategies module is private; InferenceRequest::New takes a RequestTerms and the content; Passage::Requires_Page_Images is Is_Page_Image_Required -- plus one that is new: HostedWallClock left xvpe-clock for xvpe-host-clock on 2026-09-29, so SystemClock must re-export it from there, which adopts a crate this repository has not named before. xvpe-host-clock's default features enable nothing, and its default closure is xvpe-clock, xvpe-primitives and web-time, all already in this closure; its collections feature would bring five XVPE crates and nine third-party packages, which is why XVPE made it opt-in at 7471a1c9d. With those changes cargo test --workspace passes 452 and fails only Test_The_Adopted_Revision_Should_Be_Named_By_A_Record, which D-007's amendment now satisfies, and the extractor's committed recordings still replay, so no fingerprint moved. Cargo.lock gains exactly xvpe-host-clock, xvpe-content-identity and xvpe-algorithms-hashing and no third-party package, once js-sys and the wasm-bindgen family -- which cargo raises by one patch version unprompted while re-resolving -- are held at the versions the lock already carries. KWB-114 and KWB-116 adopt at the rev the other XVPE crates pin, name no revision in their done_when, and adopt crates that are unchanged or only extended at 7471a1c9d, so this item waits on neither. XVPE is private until its owner publishes it: 726aa3fee is already in this machine's cargo git cache, and if a fetch is ever refused, CARGO_NET_GIT_FETCH_WITH_CLI=true lets cargo use git's own credentials.
items.done_when: Every XVPE dependency in kwb-platform-xvpe pins rev 726aa3fee -- including any KWB-114 or KWB-116 added, if either landed first -- so Test_Every_Xvpe_Dependency_Should_Pin_The_Same_Commit holds and Test_The_Adopted_Revision_Should_Be_Named_By_A_Record passes against D-007's 2026-10-01 amendment. kwb-platform-xvpe adopts xvpe-host-clock at that rev with its default features, and SystemClock re-exports xvpe_host_clock::HostedWallClock under the same name and path, so kwb-cli is not edited. The manifest entry for xvpe-host-clock carries a comment in the manner of its neighbours saying that HostedWallClock moved there on 2026-09-29 and that its default closure adds nothing this closure lacks, citing D-007. The comment above xvpe-clock's entry and the doc on SystemClock stop saying HostedWallClock is behind xvpe-clock's std feature, and point to what D-007's 2026-09-30 amendment says of that setting instead of restating it. kwb-platform-xvpe's inference module re-exports ReplayInference and ReplayRecording from xvpe_ai_inference's crate root instead of xvpe_ai_inference::strategies, and additionally re-exports RequestTerms. kwb-extract's src/reads_text.rs asks the passage Is_Page_Image_Required where it asked Requires_Page_Images, and builds its request as InferenceRequest::New(RequestTerms { model, role, cacheable_instructions, schema, effort, maximum_output_tokens }, content), carrying exactly the values it passes today, each under its field's name. kwb-extract's src/tests.rs takes RequestFingerprint::Of_Request's Result through an expect with a named message in the fixture that builds a ReplayRecording. Cargo.lock is re-resolved by cargo and, compared by name and version with the lock before the move, gains exactly those of xvpe-host-clock, xvpe-content-identity and xvpe-algorithms-hashing it does not already hold, and gains, loses or re-versions no third-party package; if cargo raises js-sys or the wasm-bindgen family, they are held at the versions the lock carried before. A different delta is a stop, reported with every package gained, lost or re-versioned, because it means D-007's measurement is wrong. cargo test --workspace passes. Forbidden: a path dependency or a [patch] table; a rev other than 726aa3fee; enabling xvpe-host-clock's collections feature; changing xvpe-clock's default-features setting; changing what a request carries or what any identity, fingerprint or recording renders as, or re-recording a fixture; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests; editing a record, README.md or anything outside this territory. If anything else fails to compile at 726aa3fee -- including code KWB-114 or KWB-116 wrote -- stop and report the error, because D-007's measurement says nothing else this repository names changed.

items.title: kwb-domain's Coverage is XVPE's evidence type, re-exported through the quarantine, so the four outcomes have one definition across both products

Re-authored from KWB-118, which waited on KWB-117's move to d6f075c14 -- a commit that left GitHub with XVPE's old history on 2026-09-30, so KWB-118 could never become claimable. KWB-140 moves the pin to 726aa3fee instead, and D-007's 2026-09-30 amendment measured xvpe-evidence at 7471a1c9d as differing from d6f075c14 by one doc comment moved into a markdown include, with an unchanged manifest, so the measurement below holds at the new pin. The done_when is KWB-118's, unchanged. D-020 decides this and holds the measurement. kwb-domain declares Coverage; XVPE rebuilt it name for name on 2026-09-26 as xvpe_evidence::Coverage for its mining products, so there are two definitions of one type, and two copies drift (D-017; KWB-111 measured it happening to a copied normalizer). Measured side by side at d6f075c14: the same four variants and fields, the same five methods with the same bodies (Of_Run, Has_Run, Is_Evidence_Of_Absence, Findings, Name) and the same rendered names; XVPE adds Hash and the four names as constants. xvpe-evidence is no_std and depends on nothing, and adopting it at d6f075c14 adds exactly one package. The reasons for the type's shape -- the prototype's 1,367 Barren rows, D17, D20, and why Skipped is producible but unbuilt -- are this repository's history and now live in D-020, which the re-export points to.

Cargo.lock gains exactly xvpe-evidence and nothing else; a different delta is a stop, reported with the packages, because it means D-020's measurement is wrong. items.title: kwb-platform-std's DirectoryContentStore keeps its documents through XVPE's content store over the injected file system, and refuses an address that is not a content identity instead of calling it absent
items.why: Amended 2026-10-01: 7471a1c9d left GitHub when XVPE's history was folded into one commit, so KWB-140 now moves the pin to 726aa3fee; xvpe-content-store, xvpe-file-system, xvpe-file-system-backend-system and xvpe-record-log are identical in source at both (measured 2026-10-01), so every property below holds at 726aa3fee. Re-authored from KWB-120, which waited on KWB-119's move to f45a7b085 -- a commit that left GitHub with XVPE's old history on 2026-09-30, so KWB-120 could never become claimable. KWB-140 moves the pin to 726aa3fee instead; D-007's 2026-09-30 amendment measured, at 7471a1c9d, xvpe-content-store, xvpe-file-system and xvpe-file-system-backend-system as identical in source to f45a7b085, so every property below holds at the new pin. The done_when is KWB-120's, unchanged. D-019 decides it, and its 2026-09-27 amendment measured the revision. At f45a7b085 xvpe-content-store's DirectoryContentStore counts only a regular file as held, refuses a put onto a directory before writing anything, puts through a unique exclusive temporary synchronized before the rename, and removes a failed put's temporary; XVPE's file-system port can create a directory, so Under keeps its promise without a second route to the disk; and adopting the store adds exactly xvpe-content-store. Bytes already on disk are compatible: a document is <root>/<64 lowercase hex> holding the raw bytes on both sides, and XVPE pins that layout with a test of its own. Today's adapter keeps its documents through std::fs beside the port the publication log goes through after KWB-116, keeps a failed put's <address>.staged file, which D-019 retired as evidence nothing ever read and the race XVPE's unique temporaries remove, and accepts any string as an address, so a caller's malformed address reads as a true-sounding 'not held'.
items.done_when: kwb-platform-xvpe adopts xvpe-content-store at the rev its other XVPE crates pin, behind the cargo feature KWB-116 added for the log -- which then enables xvpe-content-store beside xvpe-record-log, xvpe-file-system and xvpe-file-system-backend-system, and nothing else -- and re-exports ContentStoreStrategy, ContentStoreError and DirectoryContentStore beside the log's re-exports, adding no behaviour. kwb-platform-std's DirectoryContentStore keeps its name, Under(root) -> Result<Self, StorageError> and its ContentStoreStrategy impl, and keeps its documents through xvpe-content-store's DirectoryContentStore over the system file system; no std::fs, OpenOptions or other route to the disk remains in directory_content_store.rs. Under creates the root through the port's Create_Directory, so the directory exists when Under returns, as it does today. Every address is parsed as a rendered content identity before the store is asked anything: an address that does not parse makes Holds, Put and Get each return StorageError::Refused with a cause naming the address -- never Absent, and never false. XVPE's Absent maps to StorageError::Absent carrying the address as the caller gave it; every other ContentStoreError, including a variant XVPE adds later (the enum is non_exhaustive), maps to StorageError::Refused with a doing that names the operation, never a panic. kwb-platform-std/tests/directory_content_store.rs addresses the store with rendered content identities instead of short strings and otherwise keeps every test's assertion: Under creates its directory; bytes read back unchanged; an absent address is refused as Absent; a repeat put is idempotent and leaves one file; a completed put leaves exactly the document's file. Test_A_Write_Should_Be_Staged_And_Renamed_Rather_Than_Written_In_Place, which asserts the kept .staged file D-019 retired, becomes a test that a put onto an address where a directory stands is Refused and leaves that directory in place with nothing else written beside it. New tests there, each written to fail first against today's implementation where it can: an address that is not a content identity is Refused by each of Holds, Put and Get; a directory holding documents written byte for byte as today's implementation writes them reads back the same bytes. The kwb-store suites that open a DirectoryContentStore (tests/document_store.rs, tests/one_door.rs) pass unmodified. Cargo.lock gains exactly xvpe-content-store and nothing else; a different delta is a stop, reported with the packages, because it means D-019's measurement is wrong. README.md's kwb-platform-xvpe row names the store beside what the crate already adopts. cargo test --workspace passes. Forbidden: keeping, writing or reading a .staged file; mapping an unparseable address to Absent or to false; behaviour in kwb-platform-xvpe beyond re-exports; changing kwb-platform's ContentStoreStrategy or StorageError; moving where a document lands on disk; naming an xvpe_ crate anywhere but kwb-platform-xvpe; editing a test outside kwb-platform-std/tests/directory_content_store.rs; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests; a path dependency; moving the rev.

items.title: A citation cannot be followed from a new process, and two processes may write one store with nothing between them
items.why: Re-authored from KWB-123, which depended on KWB-120; that item was re-authored as KWB-142 when its pin target left GitHub on 2026-09-30, so KWB-123 could never become claimable. Only the item references change. Goal G1 of D-021, rows C-14, C-65 and C-81 of docs/corpus/prototype-capabilities.md. KWB-140 moves the pin to 726aa3fee and KWB-142 keeps the documents through XVPE's content store, which settles where the bytes live and leaves two things open. README.md says following a citation returns the exact bytes, but DocumentStore::Read consults an in-memory map that a store opened by a new process starts empty, and no command follows a citation at all, so a document one process admitted cannot be read back by another (C-65). And two processes may write one store at once with nothing between them (C-81), where the prototype had optimistic concept creation and a stage lock, and XVPE's cross-process lock is not started. C-14, content-derived claim identity, is met by KWB-1 and KWB-15 and needs only its verdict.
items.done_when: A record verdicts C-14, C-65 and C-81 by name. For C-65 it decides whether DocumentStore::Read consults the durable medium when memory does not hold an address, and whether a verb prints the bytes at an address or README.md's present-tense claim is corrected, saying which and why. For C-81 it decides whether concurrent writers are serialized through an XVPE lock -- specifying step X8 in XVPE's docs/plans/programs/ecosystem-substrate/kwb-parity.md to ready -- refused by a lock of this repository's own, or declined with the reason. It authors the implementation items those decisions imply, each with territory, a done_when that names what is forbidden, and a predicate that selects every crate it changes, depending on KWB-142 wherever they touch the store. Forbidden: a read that answers for a document the store does not hold, which is the D19-B incident in another shape; moving a pin; any source edit, which is the authored items' work. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: A closure's --because is recorded raw, so one control character in the reason makes the store unreplayable for every later command
items.why: Measured 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf with the debug kwb and kwb-mcp this workspace builds, against scratch stores outside the repository; docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md holds the finding as F2. kwb retire entropy --store S --because <a, U+001F, b> exits 0 and appends a retirement whose reason splits into two fields; every later kwb admit and kwb history on S then exits 1 with 'the publication log cannot be replayed: not a publication record', and the store stays unusable until its log is edited by hand. A line feed in the reason does the same across two physical lines. A reason of one U+0001 is accepted as the evidence D17 requires, because closing.rs tests reason.trim().is_empty() and trim keeps control characters. The cause: closing.rs copies closing.because into the Standing unnormalized (the two because: closing.because.to_owned() sites), while publication.rs states that every text a domain type keeps is normalized, so no field a record carries holds the separator or a newline, and the record joins its fields unescaped on that guarantee. KWB-50 fixed the same shape for --scope.
items.done_when: closing.rs passes --because through kwb_model::Normalize_Text before it builds the Standing, for retire and for supersede alike, records the normalized text, and refuses a reason that normalizes to nothing with exit 2 and the message an empty reason gets today. A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/closing_reason.rs drives the built binary on scratch stores whose directory names carry std::process::id(). For each of the reasons a<U+001F>b, first<LF>second, first<CR><LF>second, a<U+0085>b, <TAB>leading, and a<U+2028>b: a retire and a supersede each exit 0; kwb admit of a second file and kwb history on the same store then exit 0; and the closing record in the store's publications.log carries, as its reason field, kwb_model::Normalize_Text of the argument -- compared through the function rather than a literal, so KWB-111's change to lone line breaks does not move the test. For the reasons <U+0001> and <U+0001><U+0007>, retire and supersede exit 2 and the log's bytes are unchanged. The test was shown to fail with the normalization removed, and closing.rs was restored byte-identically. Forbidden: changing the publication record's format, field order or separator; escaping instead of normalizing; editing kwb-domain or kwb-model; repairing, migrating or rewriting a log already written; recording a reason that differs from Normalize_Text of the argument; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-cli passes.

items.title: A closure is published without a time, so history --as-of reports a supersession as in force before it happened
items.why: Measured 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf with the debug kwb and kwb-mcp this workspace builds, against scratch stores outside the repository; docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md holds the finding as F10. Two concepts were admitted at second T1 and one superseded into the other two seconds later. Every admission record ends in T1; the supersession record ends at its last field with no time. kwb history --as-of T1 then answers 'through 7 of 7', one concept current -- the supersession counted as in force at a moment before it was made. closing.rs appends publication.Record(None), and history.rs keeps every untimed record in an --as-of answer (Published_At(record).is_none_or(...)). KWB-64 gave publications a time so that --as-of could be asked at all; closures were left out of it.
items.done_when: retire and supersede record their publication with the instant the run read from the same SystemClock kwb admit reads, so every closing record carries a time. A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/closing_time.rs drives the binary on scratch stores whose names carry std::process::id(): each closure's recorded instant lies inside the window bracketing the command, as composition_seam.rs brackets an admission's; and after an admission at one second and a supersession at a later second, kwb history --as-of the admission's second reports the superseded concept current, and --as-of the closure's second reports it closed. The test was shown to fail with Record(None) restored, and closing.rs restored byte-identically. Forbidden: changing a record's arity or field order beyond the trailing time admissions already carry; changing how history reads a log written before this item, untimed closures included, which is a decision of its own; a clock other than the one admit uses; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-cli passes.

items.title: No test runs kwb retire or kwb supersede to success, so the closure paths are held only by their refusals

A closure is the one operation D17 governs, so a regression in what it records would reach the log with every test green. The behaviour was measured by hand with the built binary: retire and supersede exit 0, and kwb-mcp merge_losers then lists the loser with its successor and reason.
items.done_when: A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/closing_success.rs drives the built binary on scratch stores whose names carry std::process::id(), with reasons free of control characters. Retiring a published concept exits 0 and the log replays it retired with the given reason. Superseding a published concept into another published concept exits 0, and kwb-mcp <store> merge_losers lists the loser with that successor and reason. Superseding into a concept nobody published exits non-zero and leaves the log's bytes unchanged. Superseding a concept into itself is refused and leaves the log unchanged, including when the two names differ only in surrounding whitespace. Each mutation was performed and caught, then restored byte-identically: removing the self-supersession check in closing.rs turns the self-supersession case red, and removing the published-successor check turns the unpublished-successor case red. items.title: kwb history, retire, supersede and kwb-mcp create a store at any path they are given, so a mistyped path reads as an empty corpus and a closure can be recorded in one
items.why: Measured 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf with the debug kwb and kwb-mcp this workspace builds, against scratch stores outside the repository; docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md holds the finding as F11. kwb history --store ./corpsu exits 0 printing 'through 0 of 0'; kwb-mcp ./corpsu2 merge_losers exits 0 printing (nothing); kwb retire x --store ./corpsu3 --because r exits 0, prints 'closed x', and records the closure of a concept nobody published. All three directories exist afterwards. FileRecordLog::At creates the log's directory and opens with create(true), and kwb-mcp and kwb-cli's keeping.rs open every store through it. history.rs's own comment says that reporting zero concepts there would be true of the value and false about the corpus, and prototype-incidents.md's D19-B is that blindness must be loud. Only admit has a reason to create a store.

items.title: An argument that is not Unicode, or a closed standard output, makes kwb and kwb-mcp panic, so a refusal arrives as exit 101
items.why: Read 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf (docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md, F13). D-018 says a panic is a panic path, which this workspace denies. Both binaries read their arguments with std::env::args(), whose iterator the standard library documents as panicking on an argument that is not valid Unicode; and every report is printed with println!, which the standard library documents as panicking when writing to standard output fails -- a closed pipe. For kwb admit the records are already appended when the report prints, so a run that succeeded reports a crash.
items.done_when: Both binaries read their arguments through std::env::args_os and refuse an argument that is not valid Unicode with exit 2, naming its position. Every report is written through a handle whose write failure becomes a refusal with exit 1 rather than a panic, and records already appended stay appended. New test files crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/refusal_not_panic.rs and crates/host/kwb-mcp/tests/refusal_not_panic.rs: an argument that is not Unicode (on Windows an OsString from the lone wide unit 0xD800, elsewhere from the byte 0xFF) gives exit 2 and no panic message on standard error; kwb admit run with standard output connected to a pipe whose reading end is already closed exits with a code other than 101, and the store's log holds the run's records. The first was shown to fail with std::env::args() restored. Forbidden: changing the text of any report or message; catch_unwind or a panic hook; changing the exit code of an existing refusal; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-cli -p kwb-mcp passes.

items.title: No test cuts a publication log at every byte, so what a crash mid-append publishes is held at one offset
items.why: D-019: a torn tail is a refusal, because a crash mid-append would otherwise publish something nobody published. KWB-116 makes Records() refuse a log whose last line lacks its terminator and tests one such log. A crash can stop a write at any byte, including inside a multi-byte character, and at 17f82cf a cut inside a trailing field replays as a shorter name or a different time (KWB-116's why; docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md, F16). Once the refusal exists, the property worth holding is that no cut anywhere yields a record that was never written.
items.done_when: A new test file crates/platform/kwb-platform-std/tests/file_record_log_truncation.rs appends records holding ASCII, two-, three- and four-byte characters through FileRecordLog, and for every byte offset k from 0 to the file's length reads a copy truncated to k bytes: when k falls just after a line terminator, Records() returns exactly the complete records before it; at every other offset Records() is refused, and the refusal names how many complete records precede the fragment; no offset yields a record that was not appended. A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/torn_log.rs writes a log with the built binary -- two admissions, a supersession and a retirement -- and for every offset applies the same reading, then requires Replay_Records over each accepted prefix to equal replaying the same number of written records, compared on every version: value, standing, reason, successor and time; and with the log cut inside a record, kwb admit, kwb retire, kwb supersede and kwb history each exit 1 and leave the log's bytes unchanged. Every offset is covered; none is sampled. Two mutations in the adapter were each performed, caught and restored byte-identically: mapping a torn tail to Ok without the fragment, and mapping it to Ok with the fragment kept. Forbidden: terminating, keeping, dropping or repairing a torn tail, which D-019 leaves undecided; editing anything under src; editing KWB-116's tests. cargo test -p kwb-platform-std -p kwb-cli passes.

items.title: Replay is compared with what was published only by counts and current identities, so a replay that lost every reason, successor or time would pass
items.why: D-014: the graph becomes durable by replaying what was published. Read 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf (docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md): kwb-domain/tests/publication.rs compares concept counts and the identities of current claims and assertions; closed versions, reasons, successors and times are never compared, so a replay that recorded every retirement with an empty reason would pass. Three refusals have no test: an assertion naming a claim nobody published, an Unaddressed reference, and an asserted record carrying a reason.
items.done_when: A new test file crates/domain/kwb-domain/tests/replay_fidelity.rs. For every sequence of one to four operations, enumerated exhaustively rather than sampled, over two concept names, two claim texts and two sources -- publish a concept, publish a claim, publish an assertion scoped or unstated, retire a concept, supersede a concept into the other -- applying each publication to a graph through the KnowledgeGraph operations kwb-ingest's admission report calls when it applies an admission live, and replaying the same records through Replay_Records, give graphs equal on every version: value, standing, reason, successor and Published_At time. Replaying the same records twice gives equal graphs, and a log with every record repeated in place replays to the same graph. A refusal table, each case refused with its own ReplayError variant: an assertion before its claim; a claim before its concept; an address of 63 characters, an uppercase address and a non-hexadecimal address, each in a claim record and in an assertion record; an asserted record carrying a reason; a superseded record whose successor does not parse. A sweep that substitutes and that deletes each single byte of a fixture log never panics, and asserts the number of corruptions that replay silently as a different graph, as evidence for KWB-161. The fidelity test was shown to fail when replay records a retirement's reason as a constant, and publication.rs was restored byte-identically. If any case fails, stop and abandon naming the case: the fix is a Correction this item does not authorize. Forbidden: editing anything under src; asserting what a supersession cycle, re-closing or closing an unpublished concept should do beyond live equals replay, which KWB-159 decides; sampling where enumeration is feasible. cargo test -p kwb-domain passes.

items.title: Replay is quadratic in the publication log, so every kwb admit pays seconds per ten thousand records and minutes at a library's size
items.why: D-014 says a replay is linear in publications. Measured 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf in a release build, replaying synthetic logs of concepts that each carry one claim and one assertion: 750 records 4.7 ms, 1,500 15.5 ms, 3,000 121.7 ms, 6,000 464.9 ms, 12,000 2,138.6 ms -- each doubling costs about four times (docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md, F26). Read: replay looks up a record's concept and claim by collecting and sorting every version the graph holds (Concept_At and Claim_At in publication.rs, over knowledge_graph.rs's listing), and CurrentKnowledge::Assertions scans a list once per assertion. kwb admit replays the whole log before every admission, and kwb history and kwb-mcp replay it on start, so at the reference library's expected hundreds of thousands of records one admission would wait tens of minutes before reading anything.
items.done_when: Replay finds a record's concept or claim by key in the map the graph already holds instead of listing and sorting every version, and CurrentKnowledge::Assertions answers membership by key; what Replay_Records returns is unchanged. A new test file crates/domain/kwb-domain/tests/replay_growth.rs replays synthetic logs of N and 8N concepts, each with one claim and one assertion, with N chosen so the suite with the old lookup restored still finishes inside the predicate's timeout, and asserts growth at most linear with a stated margin: by counting the lookups replay performs, if the code admits a counter without changing its public surface, or otherwise by the ratio of the two replay times, each the minimum of five runs, staying below 16 where linear is 8 and quadratic 64. Never an absolute time bound. The existing replay tests pass unmodified. The growth test was shown to fail with the old lookup restored, and the source restored byte-identically. Forbidden: changing replay's semantics, refusals or the order of anything it reports; a cache that outlives one call; parallelism; an absolute wall-clock assertion; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-domain -p kwb-cli passes.

items.title: kwb-mcp neighbours does not normalize the name it is asked about, so a trailing space reads as a concept the graph does not hold
items.why: Measured 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf with the debug kwb and kwb-mcp this workspace builds, against scratch stores outside the repository; docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md holds the finding as F21. On one store, kwb-mcp <store> neighbours 'oxidation ' answers (nothing) while neighbours 'oxidation' and held_neighbours 'oxidation ' both find the concept. neighbours compares the raw argument with each candidate's canonical name; held_neighbours normalizes it first. A concept's name is normalized when it is published, so the raw comparison can only miss, and an agent told (nothing) has no way to tell a miss from an absence -- prototype-incidents.md's D19-B, blindness must be loud.
items.done_when: neighbours normalizes the asked name through kwb_model::Normalize_Text before comparing it, as held_neighbours does, through one shared function the two tools call. A new test file crates/host/kwb-mcp/tests/name_normalization.rs: for a published concept, neighbours and held_neighbours each find it when asked with a trailing space, a leading space, a doubled inner space and a tab between words, and return the same concept for each spelling. The test was shown to fail with neighbours comparing the raw argument again, and lib.rs restored byte-identically. Forbidden: folding case; changing what either tool prints; changing Normalize_Text; deciding what an empty answer prints, which KWB-126 owns. cargo test -p kwb-mcp passes.

items.title: A replayed answer is checked only for shape, so 33 propositions, empty strings and texts holding the record separator all reach admission
items.why: Read 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf (docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md, F6). reads_text.rs states that the 32-proposition ceiling is part of the request's schema, so an answer offering more comes back non-conforming and is refused; the same file concedes that ReplayInference returns what was recorded, so a recording carrying a non-conforming answer replays as a valid one. Proposed_From takes any number of propositions, and Proposed_Of checks only that both fields exist and are text. Every test in the crate replays one 48-character passage with well-formed answers, so no adversarial answer has ever been replayed.
items.done_when: Proposed_From refuses an answer carrying more than MAXIMUM_PROPOSITIONS propositions as ReaderFailed, so a reading's whole answer is refused, consistent with how one malformed proposition is refused today. A new test file crates/ingestion/kwb-extract/tests/adversarial_answers.rs replays recorded answers through the same ReplayInference the existing tests use: 33 propositions is refused and 32 is accepted; an answer whose root is text, a record, a number or null; a list of non-records; a record missing claim; a numeric concept; a record with extra fields; empty strings; a proposition repeated; a 10,000-character claim; a claim and a concept holding U+001F and holding a line feed; a recording made for another passage or another model. Each lands as Unmet, or for the empty, control-only and separator cases as whatever admission records for a refused extraction, and in every case the records admission publishes from the result, rendered by Publication::Record, replay through Replay_Records. Shown to fail with the count check removed, and reads_text.rs restored byte-identically. Forbidden: a live network call; re-recording or editing an existing fixture; changing PROTOCOL or the request; deciding grounding, which KWB-128 owns; deciding passage size, which KWB-125 owns; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-extract passes.

abandoned.reason: The cardinality defect is real, but the acceptance contract also demands Unmet for repeated propositions and a 10000-character claim while forbidding request or grounding changes. At c9fbfa4, Propositions_Schema constrains only sequence length, field presence and text types; it declares no text length or uniqueness bound. Proposed_Of therefore accepts the long nonempty claim and duplicate records as contract-conforming, and D-027 separately decides repeats are counted during admission. Making those become Unmet would add semantics the count correction does not establish. No source was edited. The count guard will be handled in a narrower required release item while preserving the separately governed grounding and repeat obligations.

items.title: Every passage's location says 'characters 0 to 0 of the text', because a page span is formatted as a character range

items.title: A later admission re-asserts a superseded concept, and supersede accepts a cycle, a closed successor and a concept nobody published, because nothing decides what may change a standing
items.why: Measured 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf with the debug kwb and kwb-mcp this workspace builds, against scratch stores outside the repository; docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md holds the finding as F1 and F14. After kwb supersede phlogiston --into oxidation --because Lavoisier, kwb-mcp merge_losers lists phlogiston; a later kwb admit of another file that --says phlogiston empties that list, because admission publishes every concept it names as asserted and replay keeps the newest version. KWB-127 asks what supersede does to a closed concept's claims; it does not ask what may re-open, cycle or re-close a concept.

items.title: A file at a content address is never compared with its address, so a truncated or foreign file there is answered AlreadyPresent for ever
items.why: Read 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf (docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md, F15). DocumentStore answers AlreadyPresent whenever the medium says it holds the address; DirectoryContentStore::Put returns early when a file is already at the destination; Get returns whatever bytes are there. document_store.rs explains why nothing re-reads: the write path guarantees a complete value under a complete address. D-014 names a half-written file under a content address as the one way the store can lie, because nothing downstream re-hashes what it reads -- and a file can be damaged after a correct write, by a disk, a sync tool or a person. XVPE's content store states that it does not re-derive identities either, so after KWB-142 the check is still this repository's to decide. Following a citation (KWB-136) returns those bytes as the document.
items.done_when: A record decides whether DocumentStore re-derives a document's identity from the medium's bytes when it answers AlreadyPresent, when it reads a document, or both; what a mismatch does -- refuse, replace atomically, or set the file aside -- and how it is reported; and what the check costs per write and per read, measured on a scratch store, not estimated. It is consistent with what KWB-143 decides for two processes on one store. It authors the implementation items, among them a Validation item whose tests place a truncated file, a foreign file and a directory at an address and assert the decided outcome. Forbidden: deleting or overwriting a file whose bytes disagree with its address without recording it (D17); taking a file's name as evidence of its content; any source edit in this item. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: A publication record carries nothing replay can check it against, and a run's records have no boundary, so a corrupted name replays as another concept and a stopped run leaves uncited claims
items.why: Read 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf (docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md, F27 and F28). Replay re-derives every record from its text, so a one-byte change inside a concept's name derives a different and perfectly valid concept, and nothing can tell. kwb admit appends a run's records one at a time; a failure or a kill between two of them leaves concepts and claims in the log with no assertion citing them, while the run reports that it failed. D-019 settled the torn tail -- a refusal -- and neither of these is a torn tail: every line is whole. KWB-152's corruption sweep, once it lands, counts how many single-byte corruptions replay silently.
items.done_when: A record, amending D-014 or D-019 where it changes what they say, decides whether a record carries the identity it was derived as, so that replay refuses text that no longer derives it; whether a run's records are bracketed, so that a partial publication is recognisable, and what replay does with one, consistent with D-019's rule that nothing closes a torn tail; the format change each implies; and what each does to a log written before it -- read unchanged, or refused with a reason. It authors the implementation items, each with a territory, a done_when naming what is forbidden and a predicate. Forbidden: rewriting or migrating a log already written; a checksum that is not the identity the record already derives, which would be a second authority for the same fact; any source edit in this item. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Two spellings of one name that render identically derive two identities, and nothing decides which differences of spelling are edits
items.why: Measured 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf (docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md): the concept named with a precomposed e-acute derives ef53c55576b9...2dde and the same word with e and a combining acute accent derives d54b4d70c0a4...25f3 -- two concepts for one word. PDF text layers and model answers produce both spellings, and ligatures, soft hyphens, zero-width characters, byte-order marks, full-width forms and words hyphenated across a line break besides. Normalize_Text folds whitespace and removes control characters and does nothing else; KWB-111 owns the whitespace controls. D-002 says an identity never changes meaning once cited, so any fold moves cited identities, and Nomos D-137 holds those values as KnowledgeReferenceIds. After KWB-114 the normalizer is XVPE's, so a fold is an XVPE step and a pin move.
items.done_when: A record decides keep or fold, case by case, for this catalogue: NFC against NFD; the order of combining marks; U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF, U+00AD and U+FE0F; the ligature U+FB01; full-width Latin letters; U+037E against the semicolon; Cyrillic letters that resemble Latin ones; U+00A0, U+2028, U+2029 and U+3000; and a word hyphenated across a line break. For every fold it decides what happens to identities already cited, reconciled with D-002 and Nomos D-137, and specifies the XVPE step in XVPE's docs/plans/programs/ecosystem-substrate/kwb-parity.md. It authors a Validation item that pins today's derivation for every case in the catalogue to a literal computed outside the code under test, and a Correction for each fold. Forbidden: folding case, which derivation.rs decides is kept; changing a cited identity without a migration the record states; any source edit in this item. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: An admission that names a closed concept publishes it again, so a reading undoes a closure that carried evidence
items.why: D-023 decides this. Measured 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf (docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md, F1): after kwb supersede phlogiston --into oxidation --because Lavoisier, kwb-mcp merge_losers lists phlogiston; a later kwb admit of another file that --says phlogiston empties the list, because admission publishes every concept it names as asserted (the admission report's concept publications all carry Standing::Asserted) and replay keeps each concept's newest version. D-023: the claims and assertions are kept, the concept is not published again, nothing is attached to the successor, and the report says how many named concepts were closed.
items.done_when: When the graph a run admits into holds a concept whose latest version is closed, the admission publishes no concept record for it, while the claims and assertions the reading carries about it are published as they are today, attached to that concept; nothing is attached to or published for its successor; and the graph the run holds afterwards equals the replay of the log. The admit report gains a field closed, printed on every run, counting the concepts the run named that the graph held closed, and README.md's admit transcripts show it, so Test_Every_Readme_Admit_Transcript_Should_Show_Every_Field_The_Binary_Prints passes. A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/closed_concept_admission.rs drives the built binary on scratch stores whose names carry std::process::id(): admit a file that --says oxidation, admit another that --says phlogiston, supersede phlogiston into oxidation, then admit a third that --says phlogiston with a new claim; afterwards kwb-mcp merge_losers still lists phlogiston with its successor and reason, kwb-mcp held_neighbours phlogiston shows the new claim with its citation, the third report prints closed 1, and kwb history's counts equal those of a replay of the log; the same holds with retire in place of supersede; and an admission naming no closed concept prints closed 0 and is otherwise unchanged. Shown to fail with the closed concept published again, and the source restored byte-identically. Forbidden: publishing a closed concept again; dropping, refusing or failing to cite a claim or assertion about a closed concept; attaching anything to a successor, or following a successor at all; changing any standing; changing replay or any other report field; rewriting or migrating a log already written; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-ingest -p kwb-cli -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: retire and supersede close a concept nobody published, re-close a closed one and merge into a closed successor, so two supersessions in a cycle empty the current graph
items.why: D-023 decides this. Measured 2026-10-03 at 17f82cf (docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md, F14): superseding alpha into beta and then beta into alpha exits 0 twice, after which kwb history reports 0 concepts and 0 claims current; kwb retire x on a store holding no concept named x exits 0 and records the closure. closing.rs refuses only a supersession into itself and into a successor the graph does not hold (KWB-37). D-023: a closing act applies only to a current concept, and a supersession's successor must be current, which makes a cycle impossible to form.
items.done_when: kwb retire and kwb supersede refuse, with exit 1 and the publication log's bytes unchanged, a concept the graph does not hold and a concept whose latest version is closed; kwb supersede also refuses, the same way, a successor the graph does not hold, as it does today, and a successor whose latest version is closed, naming that standing in the refusal. A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/closing_preconditions.rs drives the built binary on scratch stores whose names carry std::process::id(): retire on a store that never published the concept is refused; a second retire of a retired concept is refused; retire after a supersede is refused and the supersession's successor and reason survive in merge_losers; superseding alpha into beta and then beta into alpha refuses the second, after which kwb history reports beta current and alpha superseded; superseding into a retired successor is refused and the refusal names retired. Three mutations were each performed, caught and restored byte-identically: removing the check that the concept is held, removing the check that it is current, and removing the check that the successor is current. Forbidden: walking successor chains; changing what a successful closure records; changing the exit code of an existing refusal; changing the closing record's format; any act that reopens a concept; modifying an existing test; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-cli passes.

items.title: A reading that examined nothing is recorded Barren with one unit examined, so an absence of reading is stored as evidence of absence
items.why: D-024 C-28 decides this; docs/corpus/core-invariant-audit.md F8 found it. The admission report's Coverage_Of_Reading records Barren with NonZeroUsize::MIN examined whatever the reader read, and Read_The_Right_Document accepts an empty list of readings, so a reader that returned nothing is recorded as having looked at one unit and found nothing there -- D-020's own line, a rule that looked at nothing has no evidence of absence to offer, and the prototype's 1,367 rows. ExtractionStrategy already returns one reading per passage it examined, so the number of readings is the material examined, and no contract change is needed.
items.done_when: The admission report records as material examined the number of readings the reader returned, one per passage under ExtractionStrategy's contract: no reading at all is Unmet, naming as its prerequisite that the reader returned no reading; N readings with no admissible claim is Barren with N examined; a reading run that produced findings is Yielded with the findings counted as today. A new test file crates/ingestion/kwb-ingest/tests/coverage_examined.rs: a strategy returning no reading gives Unmet; three readings proposing nothing admissible give Barren with 3 examined; two readings with claims give Yielded; and a person's blank --says, one reading refused, still gives Barren with 1 examined, so kwb-ingest's existing admission tests pass unmodified. Shown to fail with NonZeroUsize::MIN restored, and the source restored byte-identically. Forbidden: changing ExtractionStrategy's signature or Coverage's type; counting extractions or propositions as material examined; any default outcome; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-ingest -p kwb-cli passes.

items.title: Coverage is computed per admission and printed, then forgotten, so nothing can tell a source nobody read from one read and found empty
items.why: D-024 C-28 decides this. kwb admit prints coverage and keeps nothing of it, so after the process ends the distinction D-020 built a type to draw -- looked and found nothing, against never looked -- is gone. The prototype kept coverage in a table it overwrote on every re-run and keyed without the model version; D-024 keeps it append-only, beside the publications, through the same record log and its torn-tail refusal (D-019).
items.done_when: kwb admit appends, after its publications, one coverage record to coverage.log in the store root, through the same record-log adapter publications.log uses. The record carries the document's content address, the reading protocol and the reader name the readings' lineage names (empty when no reading happened, never a guessed value), the outcome's rendered name, its count (findings, or material examined), the outcome's &'static str reason where it has one, and the instant from the clock kwb admit already reads. One type renders and parses the record, and parse of render is the identity for every outcome in tests. kwb admit reads coverage.log before appending, so a torn tail there is refused, exit 1, with both logs' bytes unchanged. The admit report prints a coverage-kept line, and README.md's admit transcripts show it so Test_Every_Readme_Admit_Transcript_Should_Show_Every_Field_The_Binary_Prints passes. A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/coverage_log.rs drives the built binary on scratch stores whose names carry std::process::id(): an admission with --says leaves one Yielded record with its protocol and count; one with no --says leaves one Unmet record; two admissions leave two records in file order; a torn coverage.log is refused as above. Forbidden: coverage as a kind of publication record; editing, replacing or deleting an earlier coverage record; writing coverage before the publications it describes; a free-text reason; any change to publications.log or replay; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-ingest -p kwb-cli -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Nothing here has a finding shape or a computed audit verdict, so an audit could report clean having looked at nothing
items.why: D-024 C-31 decides this. The prototype's finding model computed blind, vacuous, failed and clean, but three of its audits never set an exit code and its merge audit's blindness was an unhandled exception, and a severity filtered at display time while the verdict counted every finding. Every audit D-024 authors -- KWB-168 and KWB-170 -- needs one shape and one verdict before it is written, or each will compute its own.
items.done_when: kwb-domain gains one finding type -- the subject's rendered identity, the check's &'static str name, a reason normalized through kwb_model::Normalize_Text, and the evidence -- and an audit verdict computed from what was eligible, what was examined and the findings: blind when something was eligible and nothing examined, vacuous when nothing was eligible, failed when there is a finding, clean otherwise; and the exit code each verdict maps to, clean 0, failed 1, blind and vacuous 2. Neither type has a Default, and the verdict cannot be constructed except by that computation. A new test file crates/domain/kwb-domain/tests/audit_verdict.rs covers every combination at its boundaries, including a finding with nothing examined, which is blind and not failed. Shown to fail with blind computed after failed. Forbidden: a severity; a Default; a verdict a caller can assert; clean when nothing was examined; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-domain passes.

Declined.reason: Declined by the 2026-10-03 audit of KWB-127, and re-authored by KWB-173. Its done_when maps a blind or vacuous verdict to exit 2, as D-024 rule 3 decided, and kwb-cli USAGE_EXIT is already 2, so a mistyped store and an audit that saw nothing would exit alike. The audit declined KWB-168 and KWB-170 for the same clause and missed it here; xvpe-46, which authored D-024, caught it. Declined now because it is ready and an implementation pass would build the colliding code before KWB-173 amends the record.

items.title: No audit re-checks a supersession against the rules D-023 states, so a cycle or a merge into a closed concept already in a log is invisible
items.why: D-024 C-25 decides this. D-023 makes closing apply only to a current concept, into a current successor, and KWB-164 enforces it from now on; logs written before it can hold what it refuses, and a successor can be closed after its losers were merged into it. The prototype's merge audit re-asked the normaliser's own predicate and so could not see a predicate defect; this one checks the records against the rule as the record states it.
items.done_when: kwb audit merges --store <dir> replays publications.log through Records() and, by its own reading of the records rather than any function closing.rs uses, checks every supersession: at the position it was published the superseded concept's latest version was current, the successor was held and current, the two are distinct, and the reason is non-empty after normalization; and against the graph replayed today, the successor is current. Each failure is a finding of KWB-167's shape with its own check name. Eligible is the supersessions in the log, examined those checked, and the verdict and exit code are KWB-167's; a log that cannot be read is blind, exit 2, never a panic. kwb audit all runs every audit built and exits by the worst verdict. README.md shows the audit verb, so both verb guards pass. A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/audit_merges.rs: a store with valid supersessions exits 0 and prints its denominator; a fixture log written through Publication::Record holding each violation -- a cycle, a merge into a closed successor, a self-supersession, a successor closed since -- fails with that check named; a store with no supersession exits 2 as vacuous; a torn log exits 2 as blind. Shown to fail with the successor-current check removed. Forbidden: writing, repairing or deleting anything; calling closing.rs's checks; reading the graph through anything but the log; vacuous or blind reported as clean; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-cli -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

Declined.reason: Declined by the 2026-10-03 audit of KWB-127, and re-authored by KWB-173. D-024's rule 3 gives clean exit 0, failed 1, and blind or vacuous 2, and kwb-cli's USAGE_EXIT is already 2 (crates/host/kwb-cli/src/main.rs), the code every verb gives a command line it could not parse. So a kwb audit run with a mistyped store and an audit that could see nothing would exit alike, and a caller branching on the code would read one as the other. This item carries that 2 in its done_when. It is declined now, before the record is amended, because KWB-167, the one item it waits on, is ready and would make this claimable first.

items.title: A closed concept cannot be reopened, so a merge found wrong by an audit can only be reported, never undone
items.why: D-024 C-25 decides this and amends D-023: kwb reopen publishes a concept's next version under Standing::Reopened { because }, current to every query, and the closing record stays in the log. Because a closure moves no claim (D-024 C-26), reopening restores everything a closure changed -- which the prototype's merge-audit --undo could not, having re-derived and deleted the loser's claims, and which it did by overwriting rows and recording nothing.
items.done_when: Standing gains Reopened { because }, its reason normalized, counted current by the one liveness expression, so the existing liveness guard passes; a publication record renders it under its own standing name with the reason and no successor, and replay reads it back. kwb reopen <concept> --store <dir> --because <reason> publishes the next version of a concept whose latest version is closed, with the instant admit reads; it refuses a current concept and a concept the graph does not hold with exit 1, and a missing reason or one that normalizes to nothing as the closing verbs refuse it, each leaving the log's bytes unchanged. README.md shows the verb. Tests: crates/domain/kwb-domain/tests/reopened_standing.rs (render, parse and replay round-trip; liveness); crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/reopen.rs through the built binary -- supersede then reopen, after which kwb-mcp merge_losers no longer lists the concept, held_neighbours shows it and its claims current, and the log holds both the closing and the reopening; a reopened concept can be retired again; each refusal leaves the log unchanged. Shown to fail with Reopened counted not current. items.title: Nothing checks the documents a store holds against the coverage it recorded, so a document never read and a document lost are both silent
items.why: D-024 C-29 decides this. With coverage kept (KWB-166) the store can be held to it: every document the content store holds should have been read, and every coverage record should name a document still held -- one that is not is content lost. The prototype's coverage audit re-ran the stages' own classifier and so confirmed its own write-offs, always exited 0, and its --reopen hard-deleted rows; this one compares two independent stores and never writes.
items.done_when: kwb audit coverage --store <dir> [--protocol <name>] enumerates the documents the content store holds through the store itself, not through admission or the publication log, reads coverage.log, and reports findings of KWB-167's shape: a document with no coverage record; with --protocol, a document read only under another protocol; a coverage record naming a document the store does not hold; a Barren record with nothing examined. Without --protocol the output says the protocol check was not made. Eligible is the documents held; the verdict and exit code are KWB-167's: blind when the store holds documents and coverage.log cannot be read, vacuous when the store holds none. kwb audit all includes it. A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/audit_coverage.rs: an admitted store exits 0; a document placed in the store without admission fails as never read; a document removed after admission fails as lost; --protocol naming another protocol fails each document as stale; a torn coverage.log exits 2 as blind; an empty store exits 2 as vacuous. If the content store offers no way to enumerate what it holds, stop and abandon saying so. Forbidden: writing, reopening or deleting anything; calling admission or any classifier; inferring the documents from the publication log; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-cli -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

Declined.reason: Declined by the 2026-10-03 audit of KWB-127, and re-authored by KWB-173. D-024's rule 3 gives clean exit 0, failed 1, and blind or vacuous 2, and kwb-cli's USAGE_EXIT is already 2 (crates/host/kwb-cli/src/main.rs), the code every verb gives a command line it could not parse. So a kwb audit run with a mistyped store and an audit that could see nothing would exit alike, and a caller branching on the code would read one as the other. This item carries that 2 in its done_when. It is declined now, before the record is amended, because KWB-167, the one item it waits on, is ready and would make this claimable first.

items.title: kwb-extract asks the model directly, so no request is budgeted, retried or accounted for, and nothing could record what a reading cost
items.why: D-024 C-33 decides this. ReadsText calls InferenceStrategy itself. XVPE's xvpe-ai-pipeline, at the revision KWB-140 pins, has the caller both mining products use -- spend checked before every request, retry classification, per-role tokens, cost and waits -- and its accounting. The prototype's cost ledger dropped records when its buffer filled, summed unreported tokens as zero, made success its zero value, and was never reached by CLI commands.
items.done_when: kwb-platform-xvpe adopts xvpe-ai-pipeline at the rev its other XVPE crates pin, behind a feature of its own as KWB-114 and KWB-116 adopt theirs, and kwb-extract makes every request through its caller: the same request it sends today, so every replay fixture and recording is unchanged and passes unmodified. A spend ceiling, when given, refuses the reading as ReaderFailed, so a whole read is refused as the extraction contract requires. ReadsText exposes, for each request, a call record -- role, model, protocol, document, the outcome's computed name, input, output and cache tokens as reported with an unreported count absent rather than zero, integer cost, and wait -- through one type that renders and parses it, for the host that composes kwb-extract to append to calls.log; KWB-125's composition item carries that append. Cargo.lock gains xvpe-ai-pipeline and what only it brings, and the delta is reported; a third-party package in it is a stop. Tests in crates/ingestion/kwb-extract/tests/call_accounting.rs over replayed answers: one call record per passage, tokens as recorded, an unreported count absent, a scripted failing strategy's attempts counted. Forbidden: changing what a request carries or any fingerprint or recording; storing a prompt or an answer in a call record; zero for an unreported count; a default outcome; a live network call; a path dependency; moving the rev; naming an XVPE crate outside kwb-platform-xvpe; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test --workspace passes.

items.title: The reading protocol is a constant string, so an edit to the instructions or the schema reads as the same protocol and no coverage recorded under the old one goes stale
items.why: D-025 decides this (row C-12). kwb-extract's PROTOCOL is the literal "read-born-digital-text-v1", so a change to INSTRUCTIONS, to the answer schema or to the passage budget leaves every reading's lineage naming the protocol it had before, and the coverage D-024 keeps would call a document read under instructions it was never read under. The prototype hashed the schema alone for two of its stages, so an instruction edit changed nothing they recorded, and hand-bumped a number for another.
items.done_when: The protocol a reading's lineage names is "read-born-digital-text" at a version derived through kwb_model's Derivation from every text the reader sends that is the same for every passage: INSTRUCTIONS, the answer schema as the JSON Schema text the request carries, the passage budget (characters and pages), the answer token budget and the proposition ceiling. The model is not folded in; it stays the lineage's reader name (D-025). A new test file crates/ingestion/kwb-extract/tests/protocol_version.rs: the version is the same on every call and in every process; changing any one of the inputs above changes it; the passage text and the model do not; and today's version is pinned as a literal, so an unintended change to what the reader sends shows up as a failing test that names it. The existing test that compares a reading's protocol with the constant is updated to the derived value. Shown to fail with the schema left out of the derivation, and the source restored byte-identically. Forbidden: a hand-maintained version string; leaving out any text every request carries; folding in the passage or the model; changing the request, any request fingerprint or any recorded fixture; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-extract passes.

items.title: A visitor to the GitHub repository cannot tell what KWB is for, because nothing places the visitor page where GitHub shows it
items.why: Goal G0 of D-021. Successor to KWB-115 and KWB-137, both declined because the draft each would have placed byte-for-byte had gone false, so every correction to the draft meant declining and re-authoring the placement. This item places the draft as it stands when claimed, so a design pass that keeps docs/github-landing-page.md true keeps the placement true with it. The owner asked for the repository to be presentable to recruiters and other visitors, who should come away knowing the goals of the project. The root README.md is the authority AGENTS.md routes to for what exists, its tables are generated and checked by tests/contract, and it opens with record identifiers a visitor cannot use; rewriting it for visitors would weaken that authority or copy it. GitHub shows .github/README.md in preference to the root README.md, so a visitor page can live there and leave README.md exactly as it is. The page is prose about what KWB means and is for, which is the design phase: it is kept at docs/github-landing-page.md and kept true there. Placing it at .github/README.md is outside the design phase write territory, and that placement is all this item is.
items.done_when: The file .github/README.md exists and is byte-identical to docs/github-landing-page.md as it stands at the revision this item is claimed at, renamed there through git so the draft no longer exists and its history follows it. No other file changes: README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/records and every crate are untouched. The predicate resolves every relative link and repository path the page cites from its new location. Forbidden: rewording, re-wrapping or reformatting any line of the page (a content change is a design question and goes back to the design phase as a new item); editing README.md; adding a route to the page in AGENTS.md; creating a directory under docs. The predicate deliberately reaches nothing in tests/contract, because no test reads .github/README.md; the loose file under docs is not a directory, so the docs-directory routing guard never saw it and does not see its removal.

items.title: D-022 finds its audit watermark by commit subject, and a history rewrite deleted every Audited commit, so five finished items read as audited when none was
items.why: From the 2026-10-03 audit, agreed with the design session that wrote f9c51c7. D-022 makes the watermark the newest commit whose subject starts Audited:, falling back to the commit that landed D-022. On 2026-10-01 this repository's history was squashed into one commit, KWB: fresh history, and the reflog shows a reset to refs/reauthored/dev, so rewrites recur. After it no Audited commit existed and the fallback was the squash itself, later than every verified_at before it. KWB-107, KWB-112, KWB-113, KWB-138 and KWB-139, finished after the last audit and before the squash, read as audited, and f9c51c7 recorded Audited: none. A watermark held in commit metadata cannot survive a history rewrite; one held in the tree can.
items.done_when: D-022 gains an Amendment section and the version the record rule requires. The audit's authority becomes a register in the tree, docs/audits.md, which each design pass's audit appends to: the date, the item ids audited, and for each its verdict and any successor item. An item is unaudited when it is Done, its verified_at is later than 1790495654 -- the time D-022 first landed; KWB-122 reached back past it -- and no row of the register names it. The register is created holding every audit made so far: the first, of KWB-103 and KWB-109; the pre-loop audit under KWB-122, of KWB-102, KWB-104 and KWB-122; the second, of KWB-100, KWB-101, KWB-105, KWB-108 and KWB-110; and the third, on 2026-10-03, of KWB-107, KWB-112, KWB-113, KWB-125, KWB-127, KWB-138, KWB-139 and KWB-159, each with its verdict and successor items. The Audited: commit subject may stay as a convention, but nothing reads it as the watermark. D-022's design-pass steps say to read and append the register. items.title: Nothing here has a finding shape or a computed audit verdict, so an audit could report clean having looked at nothing
items.why: Re-authored under D-024 v2 (KWB-173): the item it replaces gave blind and vacuous exit 2, kwb's USAGE_EXIT. D-024 C-31 decides this. The prototype's finding model computed blind, vacuous, failed and clean, but three of its audits never set an exit code and its merge audit's blindness was an unhandled exception, and a severity filtered at display time while the verdict counted every finding. Every audit D-024 authors -- KWB-168 and KWB-170 -- needs one shape and one verdict before it is written, or each will compute its own.
items.done_when: kwb-domain gains one finding type -- the subject's rendered identity, the check's &'static str name, a reason normalized through kwb_model::Normalize_Text, and the evidence -- and an audit verdict computed from what was eligible, what was examined and the findings: blind when something was eligible and nothing examined, vacuous when nothing was eligible, failed when there is a finding, clean otherwise; and the exit code each verdict maps to: clean 0, failed 1, a command line that cannot be parsed 2 (the verbs' existing USAGE_EXIT), blind 3, vacuous 4 (D-024 v2). Neither type has a Default, and the verdict cannot be constructed except by that computation. A new test file crates/domain/kwb-domain/tests/audit_verdict.rs covers every combination at its boundaries, including a finding with nothing examined, which is blind and not failed, and asserts no verdict maps to 2. Shown to fail with blind computed after failed. Forbidden: a severity; a Default; a verdict a caller can assert; clean when nothing was examined; any verdict exiting 2; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-domain passes.

items.title: No audit re-checks a supersession against the rules D-023 states, so a cycle or a merge into a closed concept already in a log is invisible
items.why: Re-authored under D-024 v2 (KWB-173): the item it replaces gave blind and vacuous exit 2, kwb's USAGE_EXIT. D-024 C-25 decides this. D-023 makes closing apply only to a current concept, into a current successor, and KWB-164 enforces it from now on; logs written before it can hold what it refuses, and a successor can be closed after its losers were merged into it. The prototype's merge audit re-asked the normaliser's own predicate and so could not see a predicate defect; this one checks the records against the rule as the record states it.
items.done_when: kwb audit merges --store <dir> replays publications.log through Records() and, by its own reading of the records rather than any function closing.rs uses, checks every supersession: at the position it was published the superseded concept's latest version was current, the successor was held and current, the two are distinct, and the reason is non-empty after normalization; and against the graph replayed today, the successor is current. Each failure is a finding of KWB-180's shape with its own check name. Eligible is the supersessions in the log, examined those checked, and the verdict and exit code are KWB-180's: clean 0, failed 1, a command line that cannot be parsed 2 (the verbs' existing USAGE_EXIT), blind 3, vacuous 4 (D-024 v2); a log that cannot be read is blind, exit 3, never a panic. kwb audit all runs every audit built and exits with the first of blind 3, failed 1, vacuous 4, clean 0 that any audit reached. README.md shows the audit verb, so both verb guards pass. A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/audit_merges.rs: a store with valid supersessions exits 0 and prints its denominator; a fixture log written through Publication::Record holding each violation -- a cycle, a merge into a closed successor, a self-supersession, a successor closed since -- fails with that check named and exit 1; a store with no supersession exits 4; a torn log exits 3; a malformed command line still exits 2. Shown to fail with the successor-current check removed. Forbidden: writing, repairing or deleting anything; calling closing.rs's checks; reading the graph through anything but the log; vacuous or blind reported as clean or with each other's code; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-cli -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Nothing checks the documents a store holds against the coverage it recorded, so a document never read and a document lost are both silent
items.why: Re-authored under D-024 v2 (KWB-173): the item it replaces gave blind and vacuous exit 2, kwb's USAGE_EXIT. D-024 C-29 decides this. With coverage kept (KWB-166) the store can be held to it: every document the content store holds should have been read, and every coverage record should name a document still held -- one that is not is content lost. The prototype's coverage audit re-ran the stages' own classifier and so confirmed its own write-offs, always exited 0, and its --reopen hard-deleted rows; this one compares two independent stores and never writes.
items.done_when: kwb audit coverage --store <dir> [--protocol <name>] enumerates the documents the content store holds through the store itself, not through admission or the publication log, reads coverage.log, and reports findings of KWB-180's shape: a document with no coverage record; with --protocol, a document read only under another protocol; a coverage record naming a document the store does not hold; a Barren record with nothing examined. Without --protocol the output says the protocol check was not made. Eligible is the documents held; the verdict and exit code are KWB-180's: clean 0, failed 1, a command line that cannot be parsed 2 (the verbs' existing USAGE_EXIT), blind 3, vacuous 4 (D-024 v2) -- blind when the store holds documents and coverage.log cannot be read, vacuous when the store holds none. kwb audit all includes it. A new test file crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/audit_coverage.rs: an admitted store exits 0; a document placed in the store without admission fails as never read, exit 1; a document removed after admission fails as lost; --protocol naming another protocol fails each document as stale; a torn coverage.log exits 3; an empty store exits 4. If the content store offers no way to enumerate what it holds, stop and abandon saying so. Forbidden: writing, reopening or deleting anything; calling admission or any classifier; inferring the documents from the publication log; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test -p kwb-cli -p kwb-contract-tests passes.

items.title: A publication kwb reports appended survives a killed process but not a power cut, because File::flush asks the operating system for nothing
items.why: FileRecordLog::Append writes a publication and calls flush(), and its comment says that keeps the record from being left to the operating system's convenience. It does not: std::fs::File is unbuffered and its flush is Ok(()) on Windows and unix alike (library/std/src/sys/fs/windows.rs:660, unix.rs:1754), and nothing calls sync_data. A record kwb reported appended survives a killed process but not a power cut, and after one each file keeps its own prefix independently of the others. With coverage.log beside publications.log (D-024, KWB-166) a coverage record saying a document was read can outlive the publications it counts, and KWB-182's audit, which must not read the publication log, would pass it: lost content with a clean audit. D-014 v6 decides that an append is durable before it reports success, through XVPE's RecordLogStrategy::Make_Durable, reached through D-019's adapter.
items.done_when: kwb-platform-std's FileRecordLog returns Ok from Append only once the record is durable: after xvpe-record-log's Append succeeds it calls that log's Make_Durable, and a refusal from either maps to StorageError::Refused with a doing that names which step refused, so a caller told a record was appended has been told it survives a power cut. This needs a pinned XVPE revision whose xvpe-record-log offers RecordLogStrategy::Make_Durable (added 2026-10-03): if the pinned revision has none, stop and abandon saying a pin move must come first -- moving the pin is its own measured item (D-007), not this one. Append's doc comment states the guarantee as D-014 v6 gives it -- survival of the machine, not only the process -- and no longer says flush() provides it. A test drives FileRecordLog over an injected file system that counts Make_Durable calls by path, through a constructor visible only inside kwb-platform-std if the adapter has no other way in, and shows: one Make_Durable per Append, on publications.log's path, made after the append; a refused Make_Durable makes Append Refused; Records() still reads every record. A mutation removing the Make_Durable call is caught by that test. Forbidden: syncing once at the end of a command instead of per append (D-014 v6 names the batching remedy and its condition, and it is a port operation, never a caller-remembered sync); a durability error swallowed or logged and continued; std::fs, OpenOptions or sync_data in file_record_log.rs (D-019 keeps the log's files through XVPE); changing kwb-platform's RecordLogStrategy or StorageError; moving the rev; unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. cargo test --workspace passes.

items.title: Refuse replayed extraction answers above the declared proposition ceiling
items.why: The owner requires KWB 0.1 to admit model proposals safely. KWB-155 identifies a real missing 32-proposition guard but also requires new outcomes for schema-conforming long or repeated text. This narrow correction enforces the bound the request already declares and validates all adversarial answers through real replay without inventing a new length, uniqueness, grounding or identity rule.
items.done_when: Proposed_From refuses more than MAXIMUM_PROPOSITIONS as ReaderFailed, never truncates, and accepts 32 correctly shaped proposals. A public-seam integration test captures the request ReadsText actually constructs, keys ReplayRecording with its fingerprint, and replays adversarial answers through ReplayInference and Admit_Source. Wrong root or field types are Unmet; canonical-empty proposals are counted as refused; long, repeated, extra-field and separator-bearing otherwise complete proposals retain their documented current outcomes and every generated publication replays. A recording for a different model or passage yields Unmet. Removing the count guard makes the overflow regression fail; the implementation is restored byte-identically. Forbidden: live calls, modified existing recordings, changed request or protocol, invented character bounds or uniqueness rules, grounding decisions, canonicalization or identity changes, production panic paths. The existing extractor suite passes.
